payload.answer:
## HYPOTHESIS (final answer)

**The gardening pathway has no single prevalence style in this region: it switches style across the boundary between intensively human-held ground (Urban, Croplands) and low-elevation, moist, disturbed ground (Wetlands, Coastal, and less strongly Riparian) — and the switch is in *dominance*, not in *frequency*, which is why any one metric gives a contradictory answer.**

Garden-introduced species are encountered equally often in the city and in the wetlands — plots containing ≥1 gardening species: Urban 0.477 (31/65) vs Wetlands+Coastal 0.478 (32/67), OR 1.00, Fisher p = 1.0 — yet among the non-native species actually present, gardening supplies 55% of records in Wetlands (29/52) and 54% in Coastal (23/43) but only 30% in Urban (45/151) and 19% in Croplands (20/108), against a regional 35% (169/481). Labels: Wetlands and Coastal = **frequent-and-co-dominant** (Holm p vs leave-one-out share 0.005 and 0.061; gardening not outnumbered by unintentional, p = 0.87 and 0.78); Urban and Croplands = **frequent-but-subordinate** (gardening:unintentional 0.43 and 0.24, p = 7e-07 and 1e-10); Riparian = **frequent-and-proportional** (occupancy 0.361, share 0.365).

The context in which this habitat contrast exists is **low urban cover and low elevation**. Stratifying invaded plots by 1000 m urban cover, the azonal-vs-urbanised gardening share OR is 14.4 [2.68, 77.8] where urban cover < 0.02, 6.18 [2.74, 13.9] at 0.02–0.20, and collapses to 1.43 [0.86, 2.36], p = 0.20 where urban cover > 0.20; it likewise shrinks 7.35 → 4.07 → 1.81 as plot invader richness rises. Inside the urbanisation saturation zone habitat identity stops mattering, because unintentional (seed-contaminant/trade) introductions swamp the gardening signal. Pooling, the azonal dominance OR is 2.50 [1.67, 3.72] (p = 8e-06), 2.90 [2.06, 4.09] in a quasi-binomial model conditioned on `urban.2009.50m`, elevation and `distance.road`, 2.47–2.81 within CMH strata of urban cover, elevation and plot richness (all p < 1e-05), and 2.88 after adding 1956 cropland cover. Elevation is the strongest single covariate on frequency (OR 0.27 [0.19, 0.40] per SD; occupancy 0.360 → 0.167 → 0.028 across tertiles); urban cover moves frequency (occupancy 0.025 → 0.420 across 1000 m classes) but leaves share flat (0.31–0.37); `distance.stream` is irrelevant (rho = 0.031, p = 0.43), so the water axis acts through habitat membership, not proximity. Habitat and context are independently informative: adding habitat to a context-only model gives LR chi2 = 51.5, df = 2, p = 6.6e-12; adding context to a habitat model gives p = 3.2e-08.

**Metric dependence is part of the answer.** Frequency- and dominance-based rankings of the ten habitats are statistically unrelated (Spearman rho = 0.079, p = 0.82); restricted to invaded plots they agree (rho = 0.985), so the disagreement is generated by how many uninvaded plots each habitat contributes. Reading frequency alone would class Urban with Wetlands; reading share alone would rank Broad-leaved forests first (share 1.00 on 3 invaded plots and 4 records) — a vanishing-denominator artefact.

**Bounds.** Rock outcrops (1 invaded plot, 1 record) and Scrublands (3, 5) are **no evidence of gardening / undetermined**, never demonstrated absence; Broad-leaved forests (3, 4), Coniferous forests (5, 8) and Meadows (5, 13) are "garden-origin relics recorded where little else establishes", a low-n caution rather than a style.

Background, one sentence: region-wide gardening is the dominant introduction pathway (611/1046 records, rising 18 → 397 across periods), but that table has no habitat axis and was not combined with the plot data.

## Workflow executed
1. Granularity established in the approved inspection: `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` = 632 plots (unique coordinates) with per-plot pathway richness; `invasion_success_pathways.csv` = 81 species, no habitat identity; temporal table = period × pathway; tree unused.
2. Prevalence-style table per habitat: occupancy P(n.gard>0) with Wilson CI, dominance share with leave-one-out Holm binomial test, within-habitat gardening-vs-unintentional binomial test, intensity per occupied plot, reliability gate (≥15 occurrences and ≥15 invaded plots).
3. Dual weighting (plot-level vs occurrence-weighted, plus invaded-plot-conditional) so weighting cannot flip the story.
4. Habitat(10) × pathway(3) tested by permutation Fisher–Freeman–Halton (B = 5000, p = 0.0002, V = 0.28; plain chi-square withheld — 17/30 expected cells < 5, min 0.05); collapsed 2×2 and 3×2 contrasts with Fisher OR + CI + Cramér's V, reported both occurrence- and plot-weighted.
5. Firth penalised logistic (own implementation, validated exactly on the analytic 0/10 separation case and against MLE on clean data) for occupancy; nested LR comparisons habitat vs context; invaded-plot-only models; quasi-binomial dominance model; Poisson and NB2 count check; CMH stratified tests plus stratum-specific ORs; threshold and habitat-grouping sensitivity analyses.
6. Species-level `habitat.range ~ pathway` reported strictly as corroboration, with and without the 4 duplicated rows.

## Evidence
Habitat table (occupancy | share | invaded plots | style): Wetlands 0.500 | 0.558 | 21 | frequent-and-co-dominant; Urban 0.477 | 0.298 | 54 | frequent-but-subordinate; Coastal 0.448 | 0.535 | 16 | frequent-and-co-dominant; Riparian 0.361 | 0.365 | 32 | frequent-and-proportional; Croplands 0.207 | 0.185 | 51 | frequent-but-subordinate; Meadows 0.077 | 0.308 | 5; Coniferous forests 0.065 | 0.875 | 5; Broad-leaved forests 0.044 | 1.000 | 3; Scrublands 0.019 | 0.400 | 3; Rock outcrops 0.000 | 0.000 | 1 (last five undetermined). Intensity per occupied plot 1.00–1.77 (no habitat differences in how many garden species a colonised plot holds). Occupancy ORs: azonal vs terrestrial-natural 18.75 [9.73, 36.12] (p = 1.6e-23); urbanised vs rest 2.85 [1.86, 4.35]. Count model fits cleanly (Poisson dispersion 1.12, NB2 converged, azonal IRR 1.71–1.72, elevation IRR 0.48–0.49) but is dominated by 515/632 zeros, so it only echoes the frequency axis. Species-level corroboration: habitat.range 1.95 (Gardening) vs 2.77 (Unintentional), one-sided MWU p = 0.042, weakening to p = 0.082 excluding duplicates.

## Limitations
All models exploratory; unpenalised habitat logistic is quasi-separated (singular Hessian), so Firth was required and penalised LR tests are approximate. Habitat is partly defined by the land cover regressed on (mean 50 m urban cover 0.689 Urban vs 0.006 Scrublands), so the Urban row is context-confirming, not independent. No species-per-plot identity, so we cannot separate "garden species are poor colonisers" from "garden records concentrate where ornamentals are planted"; the azonal grouping is ecological post hoc though the contrast is stable under three alternative assignments (OR 2.50–3.61). Occurrence-level tests treat records within a plot as independent (plot-weighted versions reported alongside; CMH stratified by plot richness). Cross-table totals left unreconciled (481 plot-level vs 472 species-level, ~2%).

INSPECTION REPORT (plan only — no hypothesis testing run)

=== 1) INPUTS INSPECTED ===
All files are TAB-delimited despite .csv extension (read with sep='\t'; invasion_success_pathways.csv is comma-delimited with CRLF).

data/temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv — 12 data rows + header, no NA, no duplicates. Columns: introduction.period (4 levels: Before 1500, 1501-1900, 1901-1984, 1985-2019), pathway (AgriForest / Gardening / Unintentional), n (count). Perfect 4×3 contingency table. Pathway totals: Gardening 611, Unintentional 274, AgriForest 161. Gardening share rises from 17% (pre-1500) to 75% (1985-2019) — temporal context only, no habitat info here.

data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv — CORE FILE. 632 plot rows × 37 cols, zero NA, zero duplicate rows. habitat = 10 levels, plots per habitat: Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29. Pathway counts are per-plot species counts, very sparse: n.gard max 4 (117 plots >0), n.unint max 7 (145), n.agfo max 2 (21), n.total max 10; 441/632 rows (70%) have n.total = 0. Identity n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo == n.total holds for ALL 632 rows → counts are mutually exclusive per species, no mixed-pathway double counting. Global sums: gard 169, unint 289, agfo 23, total 481 (species occurrences, not unique species). Covariates: elevation (0–2236 m), cropland/urban % as FRACTIONS 0–1 (not percent despite docs) at 50/500/1000 m buffers for 1956/1993/2009, landscape-change binaries (progressive/regressive/no.changes), distance.stream/road (m; note UTM-like longitude/latitude 427105/4594035, not degrees), climate (annual.temperature ~4.7–16 °C, rainfall 580–1289 mm, radiation kJ/m²/day).

data/invasion_success_pathways.csv — 81 species rows × 19 cols, comma-separated. intro.pathway: Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9. 'duplicated' flag TRUE for 4 rows (stored as strings). NA only in genus.relative (79) and species.relative (77) — placeholder columns. Also has habitat.range (1–7, mean 2.2), invaded.niche.breadth, mrt, growth.form (Perennial fg 30 / Shrub-tree 27 / Annual fg 24), phylo.tip.label.

data/phylogenetic_tree.txt — single-line Newick, 3.5 KB, ~80 tips matching phylo.tip.label naming (Genus_species). Not needed for this habitat-context question; noted as available for phylogenetic controls.

Surprises: (a) files are TSV; (b) land-cover "percentages" are 0–1 fractions; (c) coordinates are UTM; (d) docs say "percent" but values are fractions; (e) success dataset (81 species) is a strict subset/aggregation relative to niche totals (481 species-plot occurrences) — the two tables are linked by species identity, not by row; (f) 'duplicated' TRUE stored as string in one file.

=== 2) LINKING GARDENING → HABITAT ===
Direct link is entirely within invaded_niche_pathways.csv: for each of 10 habitat types, gardening prevalence = Σn.gard / Σn.total (equivalently mean n.gard per plot). Quick descriptive preview (inspection-scale only): gardening share by habitat ranges from 0.00 (Rock outcrops, n=1 → uninformative), 0.19 Croplands, 0.30 Urban, 0.31 Meadows, 0.37 Riparian, 0.40 Scrublands, 0.54 Coastal, 0.56 Wetlands, 0.88 Coniferous forests, 1.00 Broad-leaved forests (n=4); Urban and Croplands dominate Unintentional shares (0.69 and 0.77). Pattern reads as: gardening relatively more prevalent in natural/semi-natural & high-elevation habitats, Unintentional in anthropogenic lowland habitats.

Cross-check with invasion_success_pathways.csv: recommended as a LIGHT check only — verify pathway label spelling/semantics match exactly (Gardening/Unintentional/AgriForest in both files) and note the species-pool composition (42/30/9 species). It cannot be used to reconstruct species×habitat occurrence (no per-species habitat list; only habitat.range count). Caveat: the species pool is dominated by gardening already (42/81 ≈ 52%), so habitat shares are partly baseline-conditioned — worth stating, not correcting for.

=== 3) PROPOSED ANALYSIS PLAN (minimal, descriptive + one statistical check) ===
a) Descriptive: habitat × pathway table of counts and shares (Σn.pathway / Σn.total per habitat) + per-plot means; visualize gardening share vs unintentional share per habitat.
b) Statistical check: 2×10 contingency test of Gardening vs non-Gardening (or 3×10 pathway×habitat) across plots using species-occurrence counts — chi-square / Fisher-simulated given sparse cells (Rock outcrops n=1, Broad-leaved n=4, agfo overall n=23 → collapse or exclude rare cells); Cramér's V for effect size.
c) Contextual covariates (limited, no overclaiming): compare habitat-level gardening share against elevation and urban.2009.50m/1000m (human pressure proxy) and cropland.2009 — Spearman correlations at habitat level (n=10 habitats) plus plot-level check restricted to plots with n.total>0 (191 plots). Optionally logistic/Poisson model n.gard ~ urban + elevation as supporting evidence only if counts permit.
d) Temporal file used only as framing context (gardening is the dominant modern pathway), tree unused.

=== 4) CANDIDATE VARIABLES ===
Response: n.gard, gardening share = n.gard/n.total, or binary (n.gard>0).
Grouping: habitat (10 levels).
Comparison: n.unint, n.agfo, n.total; gardening-vs-others contrast.
Context covariates: elevation, urban.2009.50m/500m/1000m, cropland.2009.1000m, distance.road, annual.temperature/rainfall. Elevation + urban gradient look most relevant and interpretable; climate collinear with elevation → pick one axis only.

=== 5) OPEN QUESTIONS / ASSUMPTIONS ===
- ASSUME: n.* are counts of species of that pathway recorded in each plot; mutual exclusivity verified (identity holds for all rows), so "mixed pathway" species are coded to one pathway only — no double counting, but multi-habitat species inflate Σ across habitats (species with habitat.range>1 counted in several habitats) → shares are plot-occurrence-based, not independent-species-based.
- ASSUME: 70% zero-count plots are real absences, not missing data (no NA anywhere supports this).
- CONFIRM: native-range vs invaded-pathway semantics of intro.pathway; whether AgriForest (n=23) should be collapsed into "other" for the statistical test.
- CAVEAT: garden-ornamental species pool over-representation (52% of the 81-species pool) means "prevalence styles" reflect both introduction pathway and naturalization success; we describe, not decompose.
- Small-cell constraint: Rock outcrops (1 species) and Broad-leaved forests (4) unreliable for rates; plan is to group rare habitats or interpret descriptively only.
- Land-cover values treated as fractions (0–1) contrary to column docs — flagged, not silently renamed.

NEXT (after approval): run a/b/c above in one executed script, then draft the data-grounded hypothesis answering "in what context does gardening show different prevalence styles across habitats".

payload.answer:
FINAL RESULT — gardening pathway prevalence styles across habitat types (Catalonia / Barcelona province)

HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, in context terms):
The gardening pathway shows two distinct prevalence styles structured by habitat land-use context rather than by a simple elevation or urban-pressure gradient. In production and developed habitats — croplands and urban areas (and to a lesser extent meadows and riparian zones) at low-to-mid elevation with high surrounding urban/cropland cover — introductions are dominated by the unintentional pathway (69–77% of occurrences) and gardening is comparatively rare (19–30%). In semi-natural habitats — coniferous and broad-leaved forests at higher elevation with minimal urban cover, and hydronomic wetlands and coastal habitats — gardening becomes the dominant or co-dominant pathway (54–100% of occurrences).   • Prevalencia absoluta (densidad/ocupación): densidad = media de n.gard por parcela sobre TODAS las parcelas del hábitat; ocupación = proporción de parcelas con n.gard ≥ 1.   • Bloque topográfico-climático: elevation (fijo) + annual.temperature / annual.rainfall / annual.radiation (modelos separados, no juntos con elevation).
  • Bloque accesibilidad: distance.road, distance.stream (log-transformadas).
  • Bloque cobertura: urban y cropland en 2009 en buffers 50/500/1000 m (elegir 1 escala por bloque con AIC o quedar con 500 m; las otras como sensibilidad), más el contraste temporal 1956 vs 1993 vs 2009.
  • Bloque cambio histórico: progressive/regressive/no.changes (como proporciones, 1956-2009 y 1993-2009; cuidado: son composicionales, usar 2 de las 3).
  • Modelos: (a) regresión binomial logit a nivel de parcela con respuesta cbind(n.gard, n.resto) ponderada por n.total, con hábitat como factor y luego hábitat + covariables + interacción hábitat × covariable clave, para ver si el efecto del hábitat sobre la vía gardening se explica por el contexto (elevación/cobertura urbana/distancia a carretera); (b) alternativa multinomial/Dirichlet con los tres conteos para el contraste 3-vías; (c) modelo de ocupación simple (n.gard>0) como robustez dada la inflación de ceros.

 S4. Cualquier frase sobre "hábitos" en la hipótesis será una inferencia indirecta desde la tabla de especies (p. ej. invaded.niche.breadth mediana 0.38 en Gardening vs 0.84 en Unintentional; 19/42 especies de Gardening con habitat.range = 1), no un resultado del cruce.

Eso es literalmente lo que pregunta la pregunta ("en qué contexto"). Incluye la interacción hábitat × la covariable clave. Reporta tamaños efectivos por hábitat en cada modelo.

4) AgriForest: no lo fuerces como contraste principal; 23 ocurrencias y ceros en cinco hábitats. Trátalo como contraste secundario con advertencia de poder. El contraste primario es Gardening vs Unintentional.

═══ HIPÓTESIS (respuesta a la pregunta) ═══
La vía Gardening cambia de "estilo de prevalencia" a lo largo del gradiente de intensidad de uso del suelo / presión de propágulos (cobertura urbana y agrícola, distancia a carretera principal) y su correlato altitudinal, y lo hace en dirección opuesta a la vía Unintentional:

En parcelas de **baja elevación, alta cobertura urbana/agrícola y cercanas a carreteras** —sobre todo Croplands y Urban— Gardening es **minoritaria en composición** (fracción gardening 0.185 y 0.298; residual estandarizado de Pearson −4.11 en Croplands, el más negativo de toda la tabla) mientras que Unintentional está fuertemente sobre-representada (+4.04 Croplands, +2.66 Urban). En cambio, en **contextos semi-naturales de mayor elevación, baja cobertura urbana y mayor distancia a carretera** —Riparian, Wetlands, Coastal y, de forma extrema pero con muy pocas parcelas ocupadas, los bosques— Gardening pasa a ser **mayoritaria** (0.365, 0.558, 0.535; residuals +3.30 Wetlands, +3.13 Coniferous, +2.73 Broad-leaved, +2.64 Coastal; Unintentional con espejo negativo). El contraste Gardening vs Unintentional es globalmente asociado al hábitat (χ²(18)=75.20, p Monte Carlo = 0.00015, Cramér's V = 0.280).

**El patrón no se explica por el contexto medido, pero el contexto lo modula donde el hábitat es permeable a los propágulos**: tras controlar 5 covariables de paisaje, el efecto hábitat sobre el odds Gardening:Unintentional persiste (LR=25.98, gl 6, p=0.00022) y el contexto además aporta por sí solo (LR=15.24, gl 5, p=0.0094); la interacción hábitat×elevación es significativa (LR=17.67, gl 6, p=0.0071). La modulación contextual es fuerte en el hábitat ripario (pendiente elevación +1.205, es 0.305, p=0.00008: fracción gardening 0.23 → 0.45 → 0.83 en los tres tercios altitudinales 63-112 / 132-378 / 383-605 m; pendiente urban_500m −1.028, p=0.0002) y significativa en el grupo ripario+húmedo+costero (+0.602, p=0.0018), mientras que **en Urban no hay ningún efecto de contexto detectable** (test conjunto gl 5, p=0.364) y en Croplands sólo aparece la historia del paisaje (progressive_1956_2009 +0.293, p=0.004). Es decir, el contexto importa donde la vecindad humana y la conectividad fluvial deciden qué vía llega; en la matriz urbana la composición está saturada y es contextualmente plana.

**Advertencia obligatoria sobre la métrica (los dos "estilos")**: la prevalencia relativa y la absoluta dan rankings independientes (rho de Spearman entre fracción y densidad por parcela entre hábitats = 0.115, p=0.75). Los bosques parecen 88-100% gardening en proporción pero sólo porque 3/68 y 5/77 parcelas están ocupadas (densidad 0.059-0.091/parcela, ocupación 4-7%); Urban, Coastal y Wetlands tienen la mayor densidad absoluta de especies de jardinería (0.69 / 0.79 / 0.76 por parcela; ocupación 48 / 45 / 50%) con una fracción relativa mucho menor (0.30 / 0.54 / 0.56). Por tanto: en el gradiente urbano-agrícola Gardening es una **"minoría numéricamente abundante"** (mucha presencia absoluta, baja cuota relativa frente a Unintentional); en los contextos riparios/húmedos/costeros y de montaña es una **"mayoría escasa"** (alta cuota relativa, baja abundancia absoluta), y en los bosques de altura la cuota alta descansa sobre 3-5 parcelas ocupadas, lo cual no permite afirmar preferencia.

**Hábito de crecimiento — estatus explícito**: los datos NO permiten cruzar hábitat × vía × hábito (no hay tabla parcela-especie; la tabla de parcelas carece de identidad específica). Sólo hay **soporte indirecto a nivel de especie**: growth.form × vía χ²=30.93, gl 4, p<0.001 (Gardening 20/42 arbustos/árboles y 18/42 herbáceas perennes, 4/42 anuales; Unintentional 18/30 anuales y 1/30 árbol/arbusto), nicho invadido mediano 0.377 vs 0.835 (Mann-Whitney p=0.0147) y altura mediana 3.5 vs 0.8 m (p=0.0003). Esto sugiere que las especies de jardinería son plantas leñosas/perennes de nicho estrecho que dependen de fuentes de propágulos (jardines, plantaciones) y por eso decaen hacia la matriz agrícola, pero es una inferencia a nivel de especie, **no** un resultado del cruce hábitat × vía.

**AgriForest (contraste secundario, poco poder)**: 23 registros en total, ausente en 5 hábitats; su única señal clara es la concentración en Riparian (residual +4.50, p Monte Carlo <0.0001) y una asociación negativa con cobertura urbana (urban_2009_1000m OR 0.46 por DE, p=0.070), coherente con origen en plantaciones/riberas y no en gradiente urbano-rural. No lo uso como base de la hipótesis.

═══ EVIDENCIA ═══
S2 (481 ocurrencias): χ²(18)=75.204, p asintótica 5.83e-09, **p Monte Carlo 0.00015** (20.000 simulaciones, márgenes fijos; 17/30 esperanzas <5). Residual global máximo |r*|=4.50, FWER p=0.024. Residual Gardening por hábitat (p MC): Wetlands +3.30 [0.0008], Coniferous +3.13 [0.0019], Broad-leaved +2.73 [0.0074], Coastal +2.64 [0.0081], Scrublands +0.23, Riparian +0.30, Meadows −0.33, Rock −0.74, Urban −1.66 [0.096], Croplands −4.11 [0.0001].

S3, métrica primaria n_gard/n_total (191 parcelas ocupadas, 481 ensayos): AIC mejor habitat/grupo-hábitat; hábitat añade sobre contexto LR=14.74 gl 9 p=0.098 y contexto sobre hábitat LR=5.18 gl 5 p=0.394 (ninguno aclara al otro); interacción con elevación n.s. (gl 2, p=0.473).

S3, contraste primario G vs U (181 parcelas; se excluyen Broad-leaved, Coniferous y Rock por separación completa — un solo camino observado): contexto→+hábitat LR=25.98 gl 6 **p=0.00022**; hábitat→+contexto LR=15.24 gl 5 **p=0.0094**; hábitat×elevación LR=17.67 gl 6 **p=0.0071**. OR (ref. Coastal) en el modelo hábitat+contexto: Croplands 0.165 (p<0.001), Urban 0.421 (p=0.022), Riparian 0.478 (p=0.072), Wetlands 1.183 (n.s.).

Pendientes por hábitat (bootstrap de parcelas, 500 remuestreos, logit odds G:U): Riparian elevación +1.21 IC[0.61, 2.65] p<0.001 y urban −1.03 IC[−1.86,−0.50] p=0.004; Wetlands progressive_1956_2009 +1.10 IC[0.16,3.19] p=0.024; Coastal urban −0.82 p=0.056; Croplands progressive +0.29 IC[0.10,0.60] p=0.004; **Urban todas n.s. (p>0.20)**. Escaneo de interacciones (2 gl, sin corregir multiplicidad): progressive_1993_2009 p=0.0077, annual_rainfall 0.0087, temperature 0.025, elevation 0.028, urban_500m 0.040 → lo marco como exploratorio, no confirmatorio.

Controles (632 parcelas): hábitat explica densidad y ocupación de gardening (LR 78.25 y 55.33, p<0.001) pero **el contexto no añade** a gardening (densidad LR=3.44 gl 5 p=0.632; ocupación p=0.668), mientras que sí añade a ocupación de Unintentional (LR=26.46, p=0.00007; urban_2009_1000m OR 0.69, p=0.008) — el contexto mide sobre todo "cuánto hay", no "qué cuota tiene".

Robustez: el efecto hábitat sobre G:U controlando contexto se mantiene en buffers 50/500/1000 m (LR 28.96/35.09/36.12), años 1956/1993/2009 (32.28/31.40/35.09) y con progressive o regressive (35.09-39.00), todos p<0.001; con la métrica "gard vs todas" LR=18.48 gl 9 p=0.030. Excluir las 4 duplicadas sólo afecta a nivel de especie (KW nicho 0.047→0.052).

═══ SUPUESTOS ═══
Bloques resueltos por AIC (un representante por bloque, declarado): topo/clim = annual_rainfall; acceso = log(distancia carretera); urbano = urban_2009_1000m; cultivo = cropland_2009_50m; cambio = progressive_1956_2009_50m; interacción clave pre-declarada = elevación (los candidatos del bloque son colineales: ρ elevación-precipitación 0.52, elevación-urbano −0.69). Agrupación de hábitats en 3 niveles de antropización fijada a priori (no dirigida por el ajuste). Supuesto de independencia entre parcelas (no hay efecto aleatorio de especie porque no existe la tabla parcela-especie); n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo como riqueza por vía en la parcela; prefijos = vías homónimas.

═══ INCERTIDUMBRES / LÍMITES ═══
(a) Observacional y transversal: nada de lenguaje causal; "asociado a", no "causado por". (b) Independencia entre parcelas asumida; una especie aparece en muchas parcelas y no es controlable aquí. (c) 441/632 parcelas con n_total=0 y ocupación entre 2% y 83% ⇒ las cuotas relativas en bosques, matorrales y roquedos vienen de 1-5 parcelas (no sostienen afirmación de preferencia, sólo de composición de lo escasamente naturalizado). (d) AgriForest con 23 registros ⇒ poder muy bajo. (e) El escaneo de interacciones no está corregido por multiplicidad (Bonferroni sobre 21 pruebas dejaría ninguna significativa): sólo la interacción hábitat×elevación pre-declarada y los tests por hábitat soportan la lectura contextual. (f) Discrepancia 472 (suma de number.of.invaded.plots) vs 481 registros en parcelas: no reconciliable con lo entregado. (g) Sin vínculo parcela-especie, hábito y rasgos quedan como soporte indirecto. (h) La tabla temporal (1046 especies, Cataluña) es otro universo que la de parcelas (81 especies, Barcelona): la uso solo como contexto (cuota gardening 0.168→0.752, χ²(6)=230.4, p=6e-47), no como evidencia del gradiente.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway shows a different prevalence style from the unintentional one along the land-use-intensity / propagule-pressure gradient (urban and cropland cover, distance to main roads) and its elevational counterpart, and the direction reverses between contexts. In low-elevation plots with high urban/cropland cover close to main roads — above all Croplands and Urban habitats — gardening species are a compositional minority (relative share 0.185 and 0.298; standardized Pearson residual -4.11 in Croplands, the most negative cell in the 10x3 table) while unintentional introductions are strongly over-represented (+4.04 and +2.66). In semi-natural contexts at higher elevation with low urban cover and greater distance from roads — Riparian, Wetlands and Coastal habitats, and, on very few occupied plots, the forests — gardening becomes the majority pathway (0.365, 0.558, 0.535; residuals +3.30 Wetlands, +3.13 coniferous, +2.73 broad-leaved, +2.64 coastal, with unintentional mirroring negatively). Overall habitat x pathway association: chi2(18)=75.20, Monte-Carlo p=0.00015, Cramer's V=0.280. This habitat pattern is not explained away by the measured context — the habitat effect on the gardening:unintentional odds persists after controlling five landscape covariates (LR=25.98, df 6, p=0.00022) while context also adds independently (LR=15.24, df 5, p=0.0094) and modifies it (habitat x elevation interaction LR=17.67, df 6, p=0.0071). Context matters where habitat is permeable to propagules: inside riparian plots the gardening share rises from 0.23 to 0.45 to 0.83 across elevation thirds (63-112, 132-378, 383-605 m; slope +1.205, p=0.00008) and falls with urban cover (slope -1.028, p=0.0002), and riparian+wetland+coastal pooled give +0.602 (p=0.0018); whereas in Urban plots no context variable matters (joint 5-df test p=0.364) and in Croplands only landscape history does (progressive change 1956-2009 +0.293, p=0.004). Crucially the two prevalence metrics give unrelated rankings (Spearman rho between relative share and density per plot = 0.115), so gardening behaves as an 'abundant minority' in the urban/agricultural matrix (highest absolute density 0.69-0.79 species per plot, low relative share) and as a 'scarce majority' in riparian/wetland/coastal and montane contexts (high relative share, low absolute density), with the high forest shares resting on only 3-5 occupied plots. Growth form can only be addressed indirectly at species level (no plot-species link): gardening species are mostly shrubs/trees and perennial forbs (20/42 and 18/42) with narrow invaded niche breadth (median 0.377 vs 0.835, Mann-Whitney p=0.0147) and taller stature (3.5 vs 0.8 m), whereas unintentional species are mostly annual forbs (18/30), chi2(4)=30.93, p<0.001 — consistent with gardening species depending on cultivated propagule sources and therefore declining toward the agricultural matrix, but this is species-level support, not a habitat x pathway result. AgriForest is a weak secondary contrast (23 records only): its one clear signal is concentration in riparian habitat (residual +4.50, Monte-Carlo p<0.0001) and negative association with urban cover (OR 0.46 per SD, p=0.070), i.e. linked to plantations/river corridors rather than the urban-rural gradient. Limitations: cross-sectional and observational (associational wording only), independence between plots assumed with no species random effect, 441/632 plots empty and occupancy ranging 2-83% so relative shares in forests/scrub/rock come from 1-5 occupied plots, AgriForest underpowered, the interaction scan is not multiplicity-corrected (only the pre-declared elevation interaction and per-habitat tests support the contextual reading), and the 472 vs 481 record discrepancy between tables remains unresolved.
payload.workflow: Inspection first (analysis/01-02: shapes, dtypes, unique levels, missing values, cross-file label matching, tree tip matching). S2 (03): habitat(10) x pathway(3) contingency table over the 481 plot-pathway occurrences with Pearson chi-square, standardized Pearson residuals per cell, and a 20,000-draw Monte-Carlo test with fixed margins (17/30 expected counts <5), plus per-cell MC p-values and a max|r*| FWER p; primary prevalence metric = n.gard/n.total on the 191 occupied plots, with absolute density per plot over all 632 plots and occupancy as mandatory controls. S3 (04): binomial GLMs with z-scored covariates organised in five pre-declared blocks (topo/clim, access, urban, cropland, landscape-change), one representative per block chosen by AIC, fitted as null -> habitat -> context -> habitat+context -> habitat x elevation (key gradient), with manual likelihood-ratio tests; primary contrast is Gardening vs Unintentional (three single-pathway habitats dropped for complete separation), AgriForest kept as a secondary low-power contrast; controls are Poisson density and logistic occupancy models over all 632 plots. Then (05) robustness of the habitat-after-context deviance drop across buffer scales 50/500/1000 m, land-cover years 1956/1993/2009, alternative change terms, both prevalence metrics, and the duplicated-species rows; (06) joint 5-df within-habitat context tests with Bonferroni and habitat x elevation-tercile shares; (07) plot-level bootstrap (500 resamples) of habitat-specific context slopes with percentile CIs; (08) temporal period x pathway table used as background context only. The phylogenetic tree was confirmed unnecessary for the question (it covers the 81 species, not plots) and was left out of the analysis. All steps run reproducibly with bash analysis/run_all.sh; synthesis in analysis/REPORT.md.

RESULT (all four requested items executed; scripts re-run clean from scratch in ~10 s).

HYPOTHESIS (answer to the question). The gardening pathway switches its prevalence style along a land-use-intensity gradient, not along climate: gardening becomes the majority introduction style in warm, low-elevation coastal-plain habitats whose surrounding matrix is heterogeneous and only partly converted (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), where it supplies 0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68] of invaded-plot occurrences at high absolute intensity (76 and 79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots); it drops to a minority style where a single intensive land use governs propagule pressure - Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) 0.19 [0.12-0.27] and built-up Urban (69% urban at 50 m, closest to roads, the only habitat with net regressive land-cover change) 0.30 [0.23-0.37] - because unintentional contaminant introductions dominate there (0.77 and 0.69 of occurrences). Urban is a "high-intensity, low-share" style, not an absence of garden origin (69 gardening occurrences per 100 plots, second only to Coastal/Wetlands): its low share is compositional dilution by the largest unintentional influx recorded (163 per 100 plots). Riparian is a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], statistically indistinguishable from the pooled mean, MC per-cell p=0.83) combined with a strong AgriForest concentration (13 of 23 AgriForest occurrences; standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context depresses the gardening share both among and within habitats (urban 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.91] per SD, p=0.005; cropland 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.89], p=0.002; within-habitat urban -0.29 logit per SD, p=0.018), and the joint mosaic is clearly ordered: share 0.448 where urban<=0.15 and cropland<=0.15 vs 0.245 where both exceed 0.15. By contrast elevation, rainfall, distance to stream/road and 1993-2009 landscape change contribute nothing once habitat is accounted for. Since habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context barely improves on habitat labels (quasi-F=1.67, p=0.12; beta-binomial 2dlogL=9.54, 3 df, p=0.023), the unexplained part is attributed to unmeasured proximity to the propagule source (gardens, nurseries, ornamental plantings) rather than to abiotic context. Context framing only: the gardening share of the regional introduction flux rose from 0.168 before 1500 to 0.752 in 1985-2019 (chi2=230.4, p=6e-47), so habitat differences reflect where this dominant flux establishes, not its size.

a) PLOT-LEVEL MODELS. Primary quasi-binomial (successes=n.gard, trials=n.total, AgriForest folded, invaded plots n=191/481 occurrences, 6 classes): dispersion phi=1.01, deviance 231.8/185 (null 268.6), deviance explained 13.7%, LRT=36.7, df=5, quasi-F=7.28, p=3.0e-06. Beta-binomial converged: overdispersion rho=0.0177, LRT=35.33, df=5, p=1.3e-06 (i.e. little extra-binomial noise at plot level). Habitat means with intervals (beta-binomial): Wetlands 0.564 [0.421-0.697], Seminatural-pooled 0.552 [0.375-0.717], Coastal 0.535 [0.384-0.680], Riparian 0.368 [0.274-0.473], Urban 0.297 [0.228-0.377], Croplands 0.187 [0.123-0.273]. ORs vs Croplands: Wetlands 5.55 [3.20-9.63], Seminatural-pooled 5.34 [2.80-10.20], Coastal 5.06 [2.83-9.05], Riparian 2.52 [1.56-4.09], Urban 1.87 [1.19-2.93]. Unpooled 10-level model: phi=0.98, deviance explained 18.9%, quasi-F=5.73, p=5.5e-07, but Broad-leaved (4 occurrences) and Rock outcrops (1) show quasi-complete separation (estimates +/-21-24, SE~1e4) - descriptive only. Sensitivity 1 (all-plots denominator, 632 plots): phi=1.01, deviance explained 22.9%, quasi-F=27.46, p=1.1e-16; Sensitivity 2 (AgriForest dropped, 396 occurrences): quasi-F=6.71, p=1.0e-05, all ORs unchanged (5.23, 5.70, 2.28, 1.70).

b) PERMUTATION / MONTE-CARLO G-TESTS (B=20000). 6 classes x 3 pathways: G=56.14, df=10, MC p=5e-05 (4/18 expected cells<5); 6 classes gardening vs non-gardening: G=36.74, df=5, MC p=5e-05, 0/12 cells<5; unpooled 10 x 3: G=77.22, df=18, MC p=5e-05 (17/30 cells<5, hence MC required). Plot-level permutation of pathway counts across plots: G=36.74 (6 classes) and 50.62 (10 habitats), both MC p=5e-05. Driving cells (residual, MC two-sided p; Bonferroni 0.0028): Croplands gardening -2.91 (0.0004), Wetlands gardening +2.51 (0.0023), Coastal gardening +2.03 (0.017), Seminatural-pooled gardening +1.85 (0.024), Urban unintentional +1.39 (0.031), Riparian AgriForest +3.93 (0.0006).

c) CONTEXT OF STAND-OUTS. Gardening-dominant (Wetlands+Coastal): 182 m, 14.63 °C, 645 mm, urban 0.128 (50 m) / 0.240 (500 m), cropland 0.135 / 0.218, 736 m from road, landscape change 1993-2009 +0.04. Low-style: Croplands 415 m, 13.56 °C, 682 mm, urban 0.063 / 0.133, cropland 0.621 / 0.445, 550 m from road; Urban 197 m, 14.75 °C, 657 mm, urban 0.689 / 0.566, cropland 0.093 / 0.126, 467 m from road, change -0.077. So high gardening prevalence sits in warm, low, moist coastal-plain habitats with mixed low-to-moderate cover; low prevalence sits in habitats under a single dominant intensive cover (cropland or dense urban fabric). Kept one variable per collinear pair (urban500 over 1000 r=0.95, cropland500 over 1000 r=0.93, elevation over temperature r=-0.96); radiation dropped.

d) CONTEXT-EXPLANATION MODELS. Context only (7 variables, no habitat labels): 4.5% deviance explained, quasi-F=1.57, p=0.147; urban500_z OR/SD 0.732 [0.588-0.911] p=0.005, cropland500_z 0.727 [0.592-0.892] p=0.002, elevation/rainfall/change/distances n.s. Habitat+context: 18.3% deviance explained, quasi-F=3.89, p=2.7e-05, urban remains negative (-0.289, p=0.024). Within-habitat (5 informative habitats with habitat fixed effects): urban500_z -0.293 (p=0.018) and elevation_z +0.269 (p=0.025); the same covariates pooled without habitat terms are non-significant overall (quasi-F=1.43, p=0.226), i.e. context is a within-habitat modifier while the habitat labels carry most signal. Built/cultivated vs wet-seminatural contrast: OR 0.380 [0.285-0.507], p=1.8e-06. Leave-one-habitat-out (all five informative) leaves every contrast unchanged to 2 d.p.; leave-one-5km-cell-out over the 8 richest cells keeps the WetCoastal OR in 2.43-3.01.

FLAGGED (not hidden). (1) The apparent gardening richness of the pooled remote seminatural class is NOT robust: invaded-plot share 0.55 (OR 5.34) reverses to OR 0.15 (p<0.001) under the all-plots denominator, because only 17/347 of its plots are invaded (4.9 gardening occurrences per 100 plots vs 69.2 in Urban). Coniferous 0.88 (n=8), Broad-leaved 1.00 (n=4), Scrublands 0.40 (n=5), Rock outcrops 0.00 (n=1) are uninformative individually. (2) Riparian's signal is AgriForest concentration, not gardening. (3) Species non-independence is not modelled (481 occurrences from ~77 species, no plot-species crosswalk); phi=0.98-1.10 and rho=0.018 limit but do not remove this caveat. (4) Cropland cover is non-monotone at the extreme (>60% cropland share 0.375; quadratic p=0.018), so the cultivation gradient is best described as a mid-range decline. (5) Species-level niche-breadth commentary (gardening median 0.377 vs unintentional 0.835, Mann-Whitney p=0.0147) comes from a file with no crosswalk to plots and is used only as mechanism commentary; no phylogenetic modelling was performed.

assumptions: Plot is the unit of analysis; habitat pathway totals are plot-weighted species occurrences, so all shares are shares of plot occurrences, not species richness (as agreed).
AgriForest folded into non-gardening for the primary test and reported separately in the three-pathway composition (13 of its 23 occurrences in Riparian).
Confirmatory inference pools the five habitats with <=13 occurrences; all ten levels kept in descriptive tables.
Invaded plots are the primary denominator; the all-plots denominator is reported as the pre-declared sensitivity (and it is where one result reverses).
Habitat-level means of context variables are representative of each habitat class; landscape-change trios treated as compositional via progressive-minus-regressive.
Collinear context pairs reduced to one member (urban500, cropland500, elevation); annual.radiation excluded for negligible variance.
No phylogenetic modelling, no external data, and no species-level covariates used as habitat covariates.
uncertainties: Species non-independence is not modelled: 481 plot occurrences derive from ~77-81 species and there is no plot-species crosswalk, so habitat contrasts retain species-level pseudoreplication; measured overdispersion was small (phi 0.98-1.10, beta-binomial rho 0.018), which limits but does not eliminate this caveat.

The pooled 'Seminatural-pooled' gardening excess is not robust to the denominator (invaded-plot OR 5.34 vs all-plots OR 0.15); its 10-level constituents (Coniferous n=8, Broad-leaved n=4, Scrublands n=5, Rock outcrops n=1) are individually uninformative and show separation in the unpooled model.

Riparian's gardening share is statistically indistinguishable from the overall mixture (MC per-cell p=0.83); its defensible signal is AgriForest concentration, and AgriForest has only 23 occurrences overall so that concentration rests on small counts.

Context variables explain little on their own (4.5% of deviance) and add only marginally beyond habitat labels (p=0.119 quasi-F; beta-binomial p=0.023), so the mechanistic attribution of the residual habitat effect to ornamental-source proximity is inference beyond the data, not a measured effect.
Cropland cover effects are non-monotone at the extreme (>60% cropland share 0.375, quadratic p=0.018), so the cultivation gradient is a mid-range decline rather than a linear trend.

Habitat-class means of context variables are used to characterise style differences, but habitats differ in plot numbers and in which plots happen to be invaded; the within-habitat models mitigate this and the leave-one-out refits show no single habitat or 5-km cell drives the result.

The temporal contingency table cannot be linked to habitats (no temporal key), so the rise of gardening in the introduction flux is framing only; likewise the species-level niche-breadth difference between pathways is mechanism commentary from an unlinked file.

Establishment/occurrence data cannot separate introduction from naturalisation, so the hypothesis describes observed establishment patterns by pathway and habitat, not the causal mechanism of introduction.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles according to the intensity and heterogeneity of the surrounding land use, not according to climate. In warm, low-elevation, humid coastal-plain habitats with a heterogeneous, only partly converted matrix (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), gardening is the dominant style, supplying the majority of established non-native occurrences (0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68]) at the highest absolute intensity recorded (76-79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots). In habitats governed by a single intensive land use the gardening style is diluted by unintentional contaminant introductions: Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) falls to 0.19 [0.12-0.27] with 77% unintentional, and the built-up Urban habitat to 0.30 [0.23-0.37] with 69% unintentional - although Urban still receives high absolute gardening propagule input (69 occurrences per 100 plots), so its low share is compositional dilution rather than absence of garden-origin species. Riparian constitutes a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], not different from the pooled mean) plus a strong concentration of the AgriForest pathway (13 of 23 occurrences, standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context acts as a modifier in the same direction at both scales - each SD more urban cover reduces the gardening odds by ~27% among habitats (p=0.005) and by ~26% within habitats (p=0.018), cropland cover similarly (p=0.002), and plots with both urban and cropland cover above 15% have a gardening share of 0.245 versus 0.448 where both are below - whereas elevation, rainfall, distance to roads/streams and post-1993 landscape change add nothing once habitat is accounted for. Because habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context adds only marginally beyond habitat (p=0.12), we hypothesise that the residual differences reflect proximity to the ornamental propagule source (gardens, nurseries, plantings) interacting with habitat, rather than abional conditions: gardening-derived invasion becomes the dominant style in thermally benign, low-lying, structurally open wet/coastal habitats embedded in a mixed low-intensity matrix, and a minority style wherever cropland or dense urban fabric concentrates contaminant propagule pressure. All shares are shares of plot occurrences (plot-level unit), and the apparent gardening excess of the pooled remote seminatural habitats is a denominator artifact (OR 5.34 under invaded-plot denominator vs 0.15 under all-plots denominator) rather than an ecological signal.

confirmed no crosswalk between the plot file and the 81-species trait file. 2) Data setup (analysis/02_main_analysis.py): success=n.gard, trials=n.total (AgriForest folded into non-gardening); primary frame = 191 invaded plots; sensitivities = all-plots denominator (any plot hosting >=1 gardening species, 632 plots) and AgriForest dropped (n.gard vs n.unint, 396 occurrences); all 10 habitats kept descriptively, five habitats with <=13 occurrences pooled into 'Seminatural-pooled' for confirmatory inference; Clopper-Pearson intervals for shares. 3) Models: quasi-binomial GLM on grouped binomial endog (statsmodels GLM, scale='X2', t-tests) for habitat-only, unpooled 10-level, both sensitivities, context-only, context+habitat, within-habitat (habitat fixed effects), 3-group contrasts, leave-one-habitat-out and leave-one-5km-cell-out refits; home-likelihood beta-binomial MLE (scipy, numerical Hessian SEs) for habitat means, context model and nested comparisons. 4) Permutation inference: Monte-Carlo multinomial G-test (B=20000, fixed row totals and pooled column proportions) on 10x3, 6x3 and 6x2 tables with simulated standardised residuals and per-cell two-sided MC p-values against a Bonferroni threshold, plus a plot-level permutation test in which pathway counts are shuffled across plots (habitat occurrence totals not held fixed). 5) Context characterisation: per-habitat means of elevation, temperature, rainfall, urban and cropland cover at 50 m and 500 m, distance to road/stream, progressive-minus-regressive landscape change, with one variable retained per collinear pair; two-axis style table (composition share vs occurrences per 100 plots); urban and cropland binned shares and a 2x2 cover mosaic; quadratic-term tests for monotonicity. 6) Robustness flagging and exports (results_*.csv, FINDINGS.md). 7) Temporal contingency table used only as one-sentence framing (no habitat key); RESULT (all four requested items executed; scripts re-run clean from scratch in ~10 s).

HYPOTHESIS (answer to the question). The gardening pathway switches its prevalence style along a land-use-intensity gradient, not along climate: gardening becomes the majority introduction style in warm, low-elevation coastal-plain habitats whose surrounding matrix is heterogeneous and only partly converted (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), where it supplies 0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68] of invaded-plot occurrences at high absolute intensity (76 and 79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots); it drops to a minority style where a single intensive land use governs propagule pressure - Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) 0.19 [0.12-0.27] and built-up Urban (69% urban at 50 m, closest to roads, the only habitat with net regressive land-cover change) 0.30 [0.23-0.37] - because unintentional contaminant introductions dominate there (0.77 and 0.69 of occurrences). Urban is a "high-intensity, low-share" style, not an absence of garden origin (69 gardening occurrences per 100 plots, second only to Coastal/Wetlands): its low share is compositional dilution by the largest unintentional influx recorded (163 per 100 plots). Riparian is a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], statistically indistinguishable from the pooled mean, MC per-cell p=0.83) combined with a strong AgriForest concentration (13 of 23 AgriForest occurrences; standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context depresses the gardening share both among and within habitats (urban 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.91] per SD, p=0.005; cropland 500 m OR 0.73 [0.59-0.89], p=0.002; within-habitat urban -0.29 logit per SD, p=0.018), and the joint mosaic is clearly ordered: share 0.448 where urban<=0.15 and cropland<=0.15 vs 0.245 where both exceed 0.15. By contrast elevation, rainfall, distance to stream/road and 1993-2009 landscape change contribute nothing once habitat is accounted for. Since habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context barely improves on habitat labels (quasi-F=1.67, p=0.12; beta-binomial 2dlogL=9.54, 3 df, p=0.023), the unexplained part is attributed to unmeasured proximity to the propagule source (gardens, nurseries, ornamental plantings) rather than to abiotic context. Context framing only: the gardening share of the regional introduction flux rose from 0.168 before 1500 to 0.752 in 1985-2019 (chi2=230.4, p=6e-47), so habitat differences reflect where this dominant flux establishes, not its size.

a) PLOT-LEVEL MODELS. Primary quasi-binomial (successes=n.gard, trials=n.total, AgriForest folded, invaded plots n=191/481 occurrences, 6 classes): dispersion phi=1.01, deviance 231.8/185 (null 268.6), deviance explained 13.7%, LRT=36.7, df=5, quasi-F=7.28, p=3.0e-06. Beta-binomial converged: overdispersion rho=0.0177, LRT=35.33, df=5, p=1.3e-06 (i.e. little extra-binomial noise at plot level). Habitat means with intervals (beta-binomial): Wetlands 0.564 [0.421-0.697], Seminatural-pooled 0.552 [0.375-0.717], Coastal 0.535 [0.384-0.680], Riparian 0.368 [0.274-0.473], Urban 0.297 [0.228-0.377], Croplands 0.187 [0.123-0.273]. ORs vs Croplands: Wetlands 5.55 [3.20-9.63], Seminatural-pooled 5.34 [2.80-10.20], Coastal 5.06 [2.83-9.05], Riparian 2.52 [1.56-4.09], Urban 1.87 [1.19-2.93]. Unpooled 10-level model: phi=0.98, deviance explained 18.9%, quasi-F=5.73, p=5.5e-07, but Broad-leaved (4 occurrences) and Rock outcrops (1) show quasi-complete separation (estimates +/-21-24, SE~1e4) - descriptive only. Sensitivity 1 (all-plots denominator, 632 plots): phi=1.01, deviance explained 22.9%, quasi-F=27.46, p=1.1e-16; Sensitivity 2 (AgriForest dropped, 396 occurrences): quasi-F=6.71, p=1.0e-05, all ORs unchanged (5.23, 5.70, 2.28, 1.70).

b) PERMUTATION / MONTE-CARLO G-TESTS (B=20000). 6 classes x 3 pathways: G=56.14, df=10, MC p=5e-05 (4/18 expected cells<5); 6 classes gardening vs non-gardening: G=36.74, df=5, MC p=5e-05, 0/12 cells<5; unpooled 10 x 3: G=77.22, df=18, MC p=5e-05 (17/30 cells<5, hence MC required). Plot-level permutation of pathway counts across plots: G=36.74 (6 classes) and 50.62 (10 habitats), both MC p=5e-05. Driving cells (residual, MC two-sided p; Bonferroni 0.0028): Croplands gardening -2.91 (0.0004), Wetlands gardening +2.51 (0.0023), Coastal gardening +2.03 (0.017), Seminatural-pooled gardening +1.85 (0.024), Urban unintentional +1.39 (0.031), Riparian AgriForest +3.93 (0.0006).

c) CONTEXT OF STAND-OUTS. Gardening-dominant (Wetlands+Coastal): 182 m, 14.63 °C, 645 mm, urban 0.128 (50 m) / 0.240 (500 m), cropland 0.135 / 0.218, 736 m from road, landscape change 1993-2009 +0.04. Low-style: Croplands 415 m, 13.56 °C, 682 mm, urban 0.063 / 0.133, cropland 0.621 / 0.445, 550 m from road; Urban 197 m, 14.75 °C, 657 mm, urban 0.689 / 0.566, cropland 0.093 / 0.126, 467 m from road, change -0.077. So high gardening prevalence sits in warm, low, moist coastal-plain habitats with mixed low-to-moderate cover; low prevalence sits in habitats under a single dominant intensive cover (cropland or dense urban fabric). Kept one variable per collinear pair (urban500 over 1000 r=0.95, cropland500 over 1000 r=0.93, elevation over temperature r=-0.96); radiation dropped.

d) CONTEXT-EXPLANATION MODELS. Context only (7 variables, no habitat labels): 4.5% deviance explained, quasi-F=1.57, p=0.147; urban500_z OR/SD 0.732 [0.588-0.911] p=0.005, cropland500_z 0.727 [0.592-0.892] p=0.002, elevation/rainfall/change/distances n.s. Habitat+context: 18.3% deviance explained, quasi-F=3.89, p=2.7e-05, urban remains negative (-0.289, p=0.024). Within-habitat (5 informative habitats with habitat fixed effects): urban500_z -0.293 (p=0.018) and elevation_z +0.269 (p=0.025); the same covariates pooled without habitat terms are non-significant overall (quasi-F=1.43, p=0.226), i.e. context is a within-habitat modifier while the habitat labels carry most signal. Built/cultivated vs wet-seminatural contrast: OR 0.380 [0.285-0.507], p=1.8e-06. Leave-one-habitat-out (all five informative) leaves every contrast unchanged to 2 d.p.; leave-one-5km-cell-out over the 8 richest cells keeps the WetCoastal OR in 2.43-3.01.

FLAGGED (not hidden). (1) The apparent gardening richness of the pooled remote seminatural class is NOT robust: invaded-plot share 0.55 (OR 5.34) reverses to OR 0.15 (p<0.001) under the all-plots denominator, because only 17/347 of its plots are invaded (4.9 gardening occurrences per 100 plots vs 69.2 in Urban). Coniferous 0.88 (n=8), Broad-leaved 1.00 (n=4), Scrublands 0.40 (n=5), Rock outcrops 0.00 (n=1) are uninformative individually. (2) Riparian's signal is AgriForest concentration, not gardening. (3) Species non-independence is not modelled (481 occurrences from ~77 species, no plot-species crosswalk); phi=0.98-1.10 and rho=0.018 limit but do not remove this caveat. (4) Cropland cover is non-monotone at the extreme (>60% cropland share 0.375; quadratic p=0.018), so the cultivation gradient is best described as a mid-range decline. (5) Species-level niche-breadth commentary (gardening median 0.377 vs unintentional 0.835, Mann-Whitney p=0.0147) comes from a file with no crosswalk to plots and is used only as mechanism commentary; no phylogenetic modelling was performed.

## 1) Inventory (all four files inspected; no full analysis run yet)

**data/temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv** — 12 × 3, tab-delimited (not comma), no missing values. Columns `introduction.period` (4 levels: Before 1500, 1501-1900, 1901-1984, 1985-2019), `pathway` (AgriForest, Gardening, Unintentional), `n` (int, total 1046). Balanced 4 × 3. Gardening share rises 0.168 → 0.446 → 0.490 → 0.752 (period × pathway χ²=230.4, df=6, p=6.3e-47). **No habitat column** — confirms your reading: it can only supply period/dilution context.

**data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv** — 632 × 37, tab-delimited, **zero missing values**, 632 unique lon/lat pairs → one row = one plot. 10 habitats (row counts): Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29. `n.total == n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo` in **632/632 rows** (exactly additive; compositional constraint is exact, not approximate). 441/632 plots (69.8%) have n.total = 0; per-plot max 10. Regional totals: gard 169, unint 289, agfo 23, total 481 occurrences. Covariates as described (24 land-cover/buffer columns, 6 landscape-change proportion columns that sum to ~1, plus elevation, distance.stream/road, UTM coords, annual temperature/rainfall/radiation).

**data/invasion_success_pathways.csv** — 81 × 19, comma-delimited. `intro.pathway`: Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9. `growth.form`: Perennial fg 30, Shrub/tree 27, Annual fg 24. `dispersal`: Unspecific 42, Animal 21, Wind 18. Only NA columns are the empty placeholders `genus.relative` (79 NA) and `species.relative` (77 NA). 81 rows / 77 unique `Scientific_name`: 4 rows are duplicate species distinguished only by a `2` suffix on the tip label (Eucalyptus_camaldulensis2, Opuntia_ficus-indica2, Oxalis_debilis2, Populus_deltoides2); the `duplicated` column flags exactly those 4. `habitat.range` 1–7 (mean 2.2) — habitat is only a **count**, no habitat names.

**Tree ↔ species labels: perfect match.** I parsed the Newick with a recursive-descent parser: 81 tips, 81 unique, and set(phylo.tip.label) == set(tree tips) (0 in either direction), including the four `...2` labels. Internal labels are OTTS/mrca placeholders (Spermatophyta, Pentapetalae, mrcaottXottY). 158 branch lengths, min 0.119, max 325.05, sum 4585.1.

**Cross-file reconciliation (important):** sum(`number.of.invaded.plots`) = 472 vs sum(`n.total`) = 481; per pathway Gardening 163 vs 169, Unintentional 288 vs 289, AgriForest 21 vs 23. So the species file is essentially a roll-up of the same 632-plot survey. Decisively, Urban has **n.gard = 45 > 42** (the total number of gardening species in the region), proving `n.*` are **species × plot occurrences, not unique species per habitat**. Sum(`habitat.range`) = 179 ≠ 481, which rules out the "unique species per habitat" reading.

## 2) Confirming the habitat anchor
Confirmed: `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` is the only file with habitat × pathway tallies and the only file joining pathways to environmental covariates. It anchors the analysis; the contingency table gives period context only; `invasion_success_pathways.csv` is secondary/trait evidence only.

## 3) Proposed approach (with a critique of your framing)

Your framing is right in structure but I found three things that change it materially:

**(a) Share vs absolute numbers diverge, and the "urbanisation" expectation is not supported as a monotone positive effect.** Habitat gardening shares (plot-cluster bootstrap 95% CI): Broad-leaved forests 1.00 [1,1] (n=4), Coniferous forests 0.875 [0.64,1] (n=8), Wetlands 0.558 [0.41,0.74], Coastal 0.535 [0.38,0.69], Scrublands 0.40 (n=5), Riparian 0.365 [0.26,0.48], Meadows 0.308 (n=13), Urban 0.298 [0.22,0.38], Croplands 0.185 [0.12,0.25], Rock outcrops 0 [0,0] (n=1). Absolute gardening occurrences instead peak in Urban (45) and Riparian (35). A quick probe GLM (gard vs other, among 481 occurrences, 191 occupied plots) gave log1p(urban_2009_1000m) β = −1.31 (p=0.062) and within-habitat slopes that are negative in Riparian (−7.5, p=0.001), Urban (−0.94) and Coastal (−4.7, p=0.039) but positive in Croplands (+2.2). So the expected "gardening tracks urbanisation" story is **not** what the data show: gardening share is highest in species-poor semi-natural habitats and lowest in Croplands/Urban where Unintentional dominates. Habitat-level logit share correlates negatively with elevation (r=−0.78, p=0.066) and positively with temperature (r=+0.75, p=0.086) across the 6 adequately sampled habitats, but essentially not with urban cover (r=+0.02 with urban.50m). I will test this properly rather than assume the ornamentals/urban hypothesis.

**(b) Independence is broken, so a plain χ²/CA on the 10 × 3 table overstates evidence.** Cells are species × plot records; one widespread species contributes to many plots and habitats. Min expected count is 0.05 and 17/30 cells have E<5. Plan: (i) report the χ² (χ²=75.2, df=18, p=5.8e-9) and CA **descriptively**, plus standardized residuals (Croplands gard −2.9 / unint +2.25; Riparian agfo +3.93; Wetlands gard +2.51; Coniferous gard +2.50; Urban agfo −1.94); (ii) make inference with a **plot-level (cluster) bootstrap / permutation** that resamples plots within habitat (already prototyped: it widens CIs a lot) and a **species-capped sensitivity** (each species contributing at most 1 per habitat, using habitat.range to bound) so the "prevalence style" claim survives non-independence; (iii) restrict formal tests to the 6 habitats with ≥13 occurrences (χ²=31.4, df=5, p=7.7e-6 for gard vs rest) and treat the 4 near-empty habitats (Rock outcrops n=1, Scrublands 5, Broad-leaved 4, Meadows 13) as "too poor to style".

**(c) Distinguish two statistics explicitly.** "Prevalence style" is compositional (share, constrained to sum to 1), so I will model it as a multinomial/binomial composition (gard vs rest as primary; 3-category multinomial logit as secondary), and report per-habitat absolute gardening richness alongside, because a habitat can be gardening-dominant yet nearly uninvaded. I will also report the dilution logic: regional Unintentional species (30) are hyperdominant in plots (sum 288 invaded plots, mean 9.6 plots/species) versus gardening species (163/42 ≈ 3.9 plots/species), so part of the cropland/urban pattern is unintentional-propagule dilution rather than gardening avoidance.

**Concrete pipeline:** (1) habitat × pathway profile, shares + cluster-bootstrap CIs, standardized residuals, CA (dim1+dim2 = 100% of inertia here since 3 columns; dim1 = 69.7%, separates Croplands/Urban [negative gardening] from Wetlands/Coastal/Riparian). (2) Test "distinct styles vs monotone gradient": compare a multinomial logit with habitat main effects against (i) an ordinal/rank-increasing model on a single gradient score and (ii) a 2-cluster latent-style model (BIC), plus permutation test of residual variance. (3) Context modelling at plot level with GLM(Gamma/Binomial): `cbind(n.gard, n.total − n.gard) ~ habitat` (null) then `+ covariate` for a **pre-registered short list** (urban.2009.1000m, cropland.2009.1000m, elevation, log distance.road, log distance.stream, annual temperature, progressive/no-change 1956-2009), with and without habitat fixed effects to separate between- from within-habitat effects; Holm correction across the short list, reported as the guard against the 27 correlated buffer columns; zero-inflation handled by modelling composition only among occupied plots (441 zeros) and reporting that as a limitation. (4) Secondary support from the species file: gardening species are shrub/tree + perennial forb dominated (38/42 woody-or-perennial vs Unintentional 12/30, with annual forbs 18/30), animal/unspecific dispersal, lower habitat.range (median 2) — escape-from-cultivation biology consistent with gardens as the source and riparian/coastal/forest-edge habitats as sinks. (5) Contingency table only to note that gardening already accounts for 75% of post-1985 regional introductions, so habitat-level shares are a filter on a strongly ornamentals-biased species pool.

**Phylogeny: I propose we drop it from the main analysis.** The tree has no habitat information and per-habitat records are not species-identified, so no phylogenetic comparative test on habitat prevalence is possible; it can only support a qualitative note that pathway differences here are partly phylogenetically structured. Flagging this as a decision point — say the word and I'll add a Pagel/phylo-PCA side analysis on the 81-species trait table instead.

## 4) Assumptions and uncertainties (explicit)
1. Each row of `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` is one plot (632 unique coordinates); habitat labels are plot-level classifications, so habitat groups have unequal n (29–106 plots) and are not a balanced design; plots within a habitat may not be spatially independent (no spatial error structure is possible without more metadata — coordinates exist, so I can add a crude spatial-PCA Moran check if you want).
2. `n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo` are species × plot occurrences (proven in §1), **not** unique species; therefore χ²/CA independence assumptions fail and effective sample size is ~81 species / 481 records.
3. Compositional dependence: n.total is exactly the sum of the three counts, so shares are non-independent; a rise in gardening share is definitionally a fall in others (relative, not absolute, statement) — hence the paired share + absolute reporting.
4. Severe zero-inflation (69.8% of plots have zero non-native species) and 4 habitats with ≤5 occurrences: their shares (e.g. Broad-leaved forests = 1.00 from 4 records) are statistically meaningless as "styles"; I will exclude them from inference and report them descriptively.
5. AgriForest has only 23 occurrences regionally (min 0), so the 3-way table's third dimension is underpowered; gard-vs-rest is the primary contrast.
6. Multiple testing across the correlated multi-scale buffer columns — handled by a pre-registered short list + Holm, not by exhaustive buffer mining; residual confounding between urban, cropland and elevation/temperature (|r| up to 0.96 for elevation–temperature) means I cannot cleanly attribute the effect to urbanisation alone.
7. 4 duplicated species rows and the 472-vs-481 mismatch between files: I will use the habitat file for all quantitative habitat inference and never merge the two at the species level.
8. Causality: this is a contemporary cross-section of invaded plots with historical land-cover covariates — a hypothesis about context/correlation, not experimental evidence.

If you approve, I will run: profile + cluster bootstrap + residuals + CA → styles-vs-gradient model comparison → GLM context models (between/within habitat) → trait support → a written hypothesis. Please confirm (i) gard-vs-rest as the primary contrast, (ii) exclusion of the 4 species-poor habitats from formal tests, and (iii) dropping the phylogeny.

(i) Approved — `cbind(n.gard, n.total − n.gard)` among occupied plots is the primary contrast. Keep the 3-category multinomial as secondary only, reported with an explicit power caveat (AgriForest n=23).
(ii) Approved — restrict formal tests to habitats with ≥13 occurrences, but do not delete the four species-poor habitats: report them descriptively in the same table with occurrence counts and CI widths, and state plainly how the headline ranking changes if Broad-leaved (share 1.00 on n=4) and Coniferous (0.875, n=8) forests are included. (iii) Approved — exclude the phylogeny from the habitat inference. Skip the Pagel/phylo-PCA side analysis; a one-line qualitative note that pathway differences may be phylogenetically structured on the 81-species table is enough.

Four additions I want, all cheap and all aimed at the word "context" in the question:

1. Styles vs gradient is the crux — give it a real test, not just a BIC number. I want (a) the permutation/cluster-bootstrap null for residual dispersion of gardening share, (b) the ordered-gradient model (single score, e.g. elevation or a PCA axis) compared by BIC/AIC to the habitat-main-effects model, and (c) a statement of which wins. If a single low-elevation/warm-humid axis explains most of the habitat separation, then "prevalence styles" is really a context gradient, and the hypothesis should say so rather than asserting discrete types. Please also report the habitat-level correlation matrix among candidate axis scores (elevation, temperature, rainfall, distance.stream, urban, cropland) so we can see how far collinearity (elevation–temperature r≈−0.96) limits the attribution, and name that as an unresolvable confound if it stays above |r|≈0.9.

2. Separate between- from within-habitat effects explicitly, since your probes already diverge (habitat-level share rises with warmth, within-habitat urban slopes are mostly negative). Report both coefficients side by side and interpret the divergence — my reading is that habitat-level gardening dominance reflects the species pool that escapes into each habitat, whereas a negative within-habitat urban slope reflects local dilution/persistence of escapes. Confirm or reject that with the numbers.

3. Quantify the dilution alternative rather than only mentioning it. Compute per-pathway invaded-plots-per-species (you have 9.6 vs 3.9 vs ~1.0 for AgriForest) and run at least one sensitivity that removes the hyperdominant unintentional records (e.g. cap each species' contribution per habitat, or drop the top-N most widespread unintentional species) and re-runs the habitat share ranking. State whether the Croplands/Urban gardening deficit survives — that decides whether the answer is "gardening avoided in the cropland/urban matrix" or "unintentional contaminants swamp it".

4. Close the loop on trait support in one compact table: gardening species' growth form / habitat.range / dispersal vs the other pathways, plus which habitat types the gardening species actually occupy, so the escape-from-cultivation mechanism (gardens as source, riparian/coastal/warm low-elevation habitats as sinks) is either evidenced or dropped from the hypothesis.

Keep the pre-registered short covariate list plus Holm; no buffer mining. Keep the two-file non-merge rule and treat the 472 vs 481 discrepancy as a limitation, not something to reconcile.

payload.answer:
INSPECTION COMPLETE (no modelling run yet). Here is what the four files actually contain, what can and cannot be tested, and the analysis plan I propose.

=====================================================
1) FILE INVENTORY
=====================================================
A. temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv — TAB-delimited (despite .csv), 12 rows x 3 cols, 0 missing.
   introduction.period (4 levels: Before 1500, 1501-1900, 1901-1984, 1985-2019) x pathway (3: AgriForest, Gardening, Unintentional), n = species counts. Grand total 1046 introductions. Row x col totals: Before1500 107, 1501-1900 121, 1901-1984 290, 1985-2019 528. Gardening = 18 -> 54 -> 142 -> 397. chi2(6)=230.4, p=6e-47 (pathway mix changes strongly through time; recent flora is gardening-dominated).

B. phylogenetic_tree.txt — single-line Newick, ultrametric-looking, rooted at "Spermatophyta" (Pinus_radiata basal), 17 labelled internal nodes (mrcaott...ott..., Open-Trees style), 81 tips. I parsed it with a custom regex/recursive reader (no ete3/Bio/ape installed): 81 unique tips, EXACT 1:1 match with invasion_success_pathways.phylo.tip.label (0 unmatched either way). The 4 "2"-suffixed tips (Opuntia_ficus-indica2, Populus_deltoides2, Oxalis_debilis2, Eucalyptus_camaldulensis2) correspond exactly to the 4 duplicated=TRUE rows.

C. invasion_success_pathways.csv — comma-delimited, 81 rows x 19 cols. UNIT = species x pathway, NOT species: 81 records but only 77 unique Scientific_name; the 4 duplicated rows are genuine multi-pathway species (Eucalyptus camaldulensis AgriForest+Gardening, Opuntia ficus-indica AgriForest+Gardening, Oxalis debilis Gardening+Unintentional, Populus deltoides AgriForest+Gardening), each given its own tree tip; duplicated=TRUE flags the second copy. genus.relative (2 non-NA: Calamagrostis for Jarava plumosa, Rheum for Rumex cristatus) and species.relative (4 non-NA) are tree-pruning metadata, not ecology -> drop. All other columns complete. Levels: intro.pathway {Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9}; growth.form {Perennial fg 30, Shrub/tree 27, Annual fg 24}; dispersal {Unspecific 42, Animal 21, Wind 18}; vegetative {No 46, Yes 35}; 33 families, 61 genera. No duplicate species x pathway pairs.

D. invaded_niche_pathways.csv — TAB-delimited, 632 rows x 37 cols, ZERO missing values, no duplicate rows, no duplicate coordinates. UNIT = PLOT (one row per sampled plot), confirmed by: unique lat/long pairs (UTM eastings 368645-481175, northings 4562825-4684875, i.e. projected metres for Catalonia despite the "longitude/latitude" names); 10 habitat types (Croplands 92, Scrublands 106, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29).
   n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo/n.total are PLOT-LEVEL species richness per pathway: n.total = n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo for all rows (verified), values 0-10, and 441/632 plots have n.total=0 (only 191 plots hold >=1 of the 77 focal species). Column sums are 169 / 289 / 23 (=481 occurrences), versus sum(number.of.invaded.plots) in the species file = 163 / 288 / 21 (=472). Same order of magnitude and same pathway ranking, so the niche file is the plot-by-species incidence matrix of the SAME 77-species list collapsed by pathway, but the residual difference (9 occurrences; likely multi-pathway species counted twice, or plots outside this 632 subset) means the two files cannot be re-joined exactly. There is NO species x plot matrix, no plot ID.
   Land cover: cropland/urban as FRACTIONS (0-1, not %) for 1956/1993/2009 x 50/500/1000 m (means: urban rises 0.040->0.082->0.111 at 50 m; cropland falls 0.308->0.230->0.170 - the classic Mediterranean urbanisation + farmland-abandonment trajectory). Landscape-change columns exist ONLY at the 50 m buffer. Covariates: elevation, distance.stream, distance.road, annual.temperature/rainfall/radiation.

IMPORTANT DATA-DOCUMENTATION DEFECT I found: the provided "progressive/regressive/no.changes" columns do NOT behave as the metadata says. Row sums are ~1 (125/632 rows deviate), so they are complementary area fractions, but progressive.1956.2009.50m correlates NEGATIVELY with (urban2009-urban1956) (r=-0.20) and with (cropland change) (r=-0.41), and positively with the change in NATURAL (non-urban non-cropland) cover (r=+0.66); regressive correlates +0.65 with urban increase. So "progressive" = progressive naturalisation/vegetation recovery (farmland abandonment), "regressive" = regression of natural vegetation i.e. artificialisation - the opposite of the written description. The three columns are also not exactly reconstructible from the two cover pairs, so they come from the full land-cover map. I will therefore derive my own change variables (delta_urban, delta_cropland, delta_natural = 1-urban-cropland) from the raw cover columns and use the supplied categories only as a cross-check.

=====================================================
2) WHAT CAN TEST THE QUESTION, AND THE UNIT QUESTION
=====================================================
You are right: invaded_niche_pathways.csv is the only file that couples land use to invasion, and it is PLOT-level. The pathway columns are the response side (richness of Gardening/Unintentional/AgriForest species per plot), so the correct unit is "pathway-specific species richness per plot", analysed as a multinomial/competing-risks response with plot as the observational unit. Because 70% of plots have zero species, I will model (a) occupancy and (b) pathway composition conditional on >=1 species (191 plots), and report both. The near-match between plot sums (169/289/23) and species-file invaded-plot sums (163/288/21) is the bridge between the plot world and the species world; it is approximate, not exact.

Descriptive confirmation (Spearman, plot-level, 2009 cover): n.total rho = 0.445/0.548/0.531 at 50/500/1000 m; n.unint 0.403/0.497/0.487; n.gard 0.325/0.395/0.376; n.agfo 0.078/0.113/0.098. Cropland is far weaker (0.16-0.22). 500 m is already the strongest scale. Composition shifts too: quartiles of urban.2009.500m (occupied plots) go 53.9% -> 54.0% -> 62.7% -> 68.6% Unintentional share. Habitat "Urban" plots (mean urban cover 0.57 at 500 m) hold 151 of 481 occurrences, 68.9% Unintentional; Croplands 76.9%; Wetlands/Coastal are gardening-dominated (55.8%/53.5%). So the first signal is "urban + unintentional", but it must be established with a model that separates "more species overall" from "a specific pathway".

=====================================================
3) AVAILABLE SIGNALS
=====================================================
Urbanisation signal: BOTH absolute cover (urban 1956/1993/2009 x 50/500/1000 m) and change (delta_urban 1956->2009 and 1993->2009, plus the supplied progressive/regressive/no-change fractions, 50 m only). Caveat: change categories are 50 m only and semantically mislabelled; delta_urban is available at all three buffers (389/632 plots gained urban at 500 m).
Invasion "type" usable against urbanisation: ONLY introduction pathway (the plot file has pathway counts and nothing else). Growth form, dispersal, vegetative reproduction, height, MRT, niche breadth, family and phylogeny exist at species level only and CANNOT be regressed on plot urban cover (no species x plot matrix). I will therefore answer the question in two linked steps: (i) plot-level pathway response to urbanisation, (ii) species-level demonstration that the pathway favoured by urbanisation is a coherent biological "type" (pathway x growth form chi2=30.9, p=3e-6: Unintentional = 18/30 annual forbs, 1 shrub/tree, mean height 0.8 m; AgriForest = 6/9 shrubs/trees, 10 m; Gardening = 38/42 perennial forb + shrub/tree; dispersal not associated, chi2=3.8, p=0.43). That chain lets me name the "type" honestly (unintentional, low annual ruderal forbs) without over-claiming a plot-level trait model. temporal_trends gives the supply-side context (Gardening dominates recent introductions overall, so a Unintentional win inside urban plots is a real establishment effect, not just propagule pressure).

=====================================================
4) PROPOSED APPROACH
=====================================================
R1 Response: per-plot pathway count vector (n.gard, n.unint, n.agfo).
R2 Main model: multinomial "Poisson trick" (statsmodels GLM Poisson on the 191-plot x 3-pathway long form with plot fixed effects, equivalently MNLogit), i.e. a Poisson log-linear model of pathway use with plot offsets - this tests pathway SPECIFICITY (differential response), not just richness. Predictors: log1p-scaled urban cover, cropland cover, elevation, annual temperature/rainfall/radiation, log distance to road/stream, and the urban x habitat-type and urban x delta_urban interactions. AgriForest is sparse (9 species, 23 occurrences) -> report it as a third level with explicit caution (and a Unintentional-vs-Gardening pairwise binomial GLM as the primary robustness check).
