payload.answer:
## ОТВЕТ НА ВОПРОС (итоговая гипотеза)

**Городское землепользование значимо смещает СОСТАВ интродукционных pathway** (joint `pathway × urban.2009.500m` F=7.32, p=7e-4; для `delta_urban.1000m` F=6.93, p=1e-3). Внутри состава зависимости разные:

**(i) 'Gardening' — зависит от урбанизации исторически-временнó, а НЕ локально.** Доля выросла 0.168 [0.109–0.250] → 0.752 [0.713–0.787] (Before 1500 → 1985-2019), OR/период = 2.30 [1.99–2.65], p=6e-30. Но по участкам связь с городским покрытием нулевая: β = **−0.036 [−0.090; +0.017]** (M3), r(n.gard, urban.2009.500m) = −0.035. Т.е. город создаёт поток декоративных интродукций, но не концентрирует их в инвентаризованных plot'ах (правдоподобно — остаются в садах вне сети).

**(ii) 'Unintentional' — единственный pathway с положительным наклоном к фактическому городскому покрытию, но сигнал слабый.** β = +0.032…+0.033 на 10 п.п. покрытия; предсказанная доля 0.543 → 0.642 между квартилями urban.2009.500m; bootstrap ΔShare(Q3−Q1) = **+0.101 [+0.035; +0.173]**. Оговорки: собственная значимость теряется при контроле ковариат (M2 p=0.074, M3 p=0.128; 0/18 значимых в чувствительности), **три разности долей суммируются в 0** (+0.101 −0.050 −0.051 ≈ 0), т.е. часть роста — зеркало схлопывания AgriForest, и тот же знак повторяется на cropland (β>0 в 18/18, медиана +0.033) → это отклик на открытые/нарушенные местообитания, а не доказанный именно городской сигнал.

**(iii) 'AgriForest' — единственный pathway с надёжной ОБРАТНОЙ связью и она специфична для urban.** β = **−0.255 [−0.429; −0.082]** p=0.0039 (M3, +habitat); `delta_urban.1000m` β = −0.368 [−0.612; −0.124] p=0.003. На cropland эффект почти исчезает (медиана β = −0.026 против −0.312 для urban). Временнóй тренд: доля 0.514 → 0.061, OR/период 0.39, Fisher p=3.6e-27 (n=161 — единственный мощный источник по AgriForest). Причинных заявлений не делаем (23 records на 21 plot'е).

**Чего данные НЕ поддерживают:** «Gardening связан с urban в пространстве участков»; любую причинность (period — только прокси); объединение 1046 записей contingency и 81 вида в одну вселенную; PGLS (в invasion_success_pathways.csv 0 переменных ландшафта и нет ключа вид↔plot).

## Выполненные требования

**1) Оба варианта контроля — рядом, β/CI/p (β на +10 п.п. покрытия, `urban.2009.500m`, quasi-Poisson):**

| модель | Unintentional | Gardening | AgriForest | joint F (p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 без ковариат | +0.033 [0.001;0.066] p=.043 | −0.035 [−0.081;0.010] | −0.254 [−0.422;−0.085] p=.003 | 7.53 (.001) |
| M2 ковариаты, **без habitat** | +0.033 [−0.003;0.068] | −0.036 [−0.085;0.012] | −0.255 [−0.426;−0.084] p=.003 | 7.45 (.001) |
| M3 ковариаты, **с habitat** | +0.032 [−0.009;0.074] | −0.036 [−0.090;0.017] | −0.255 [−0.429;−0.082] p=.004 | 7.32 (.001) |
| M4 **без plot'ов habitat=='Urban'** | +0.021 [−0.045;0.087] | −0.007 [−0.085;0.071] | −0.204 [−0.424;0.017] p=.070 | 2.00 (.137) |

Контроль habitat сдвигает β менее чем на 0.002 → **урban-эффект существует внутри типов местообитаний, а не «мы просто считаем в городе»**. M4 (137 plot'ов, 330 records) сохраняет знак AgriForest, но теряет значимость — это мощность, а не смена вывода.

**Отдельно важно (богатство ≠ состав):** вероятность найти хоть один инвайдный вид растёт с покрытием (binomial на всех 632: β=+0.266 [0.152;0.381], OR=1.31/10п.п.), **но с habitat исчезает** (β=+0.062 [−0.078;0.201] p=0.39). Значит «в городах больше инвазий» — артефакт класса местообитания; устойчив только сдвиг состава.

**2) Предсказанный состав** (M3, средние по plot'ам): urban.2009.500m=0.05 (Q1) → Unint 0.543 / Gard 0.381 / Agfo 0.076; =0.49 (Q3) → 0.642 / 0.333 / 0.025 (на max=1.0: 0.728/0.266/0.007). Bootstrap-разности в п.2 выше.

**3) AgriForest — честно про мощность:** таблица `table9_agriforest_power.csv`: 50m β=−0.069 (MDE80=0.148) — НЕ разрешим; 500m β=−0.255 (MDE80=0.248) — разрешим впритык; 1000m β=−0.334 (MDE80=0.294) — разрешим; без Urban-plot'ов β=−0.204 (MDE80=0.315) — не разрешим. CI шириной в ~3-кратную долю. Основной источник по AgriForest — contingency (n=161), plot-данные только подтверждают направление.

**4) Шаг C решён через знак delta:** corr(`regressive.1956.2009.50m`, urban.2009.50m − urban.1956.50m) = **+0.649**, corr(`progressive.1956.2009.50m`, …) = **−0.201** → ярлык 'progressive' в данных = сокращение застройки/пашни, вопреки datasets.json. Формулировки идут по `delta_urban`; ярлыки — только подписи. Δ и категории согласованы: Δ500m β(Agfo)=−0.300 p=.008 (joint p=.003), Δ1000m −0.368 p=.003 (joint p=.001), в 50-м буфере всё ns (застройка меняется у <25% plot'ов), категории prog/regr тоже ns — т.е. 50-е буферы информативны по Δ, но не по категориям.

**5) Чувствительность (9 буфер×год × {urban, cropland} × {без/с habitat} = 36 прогонов, compact-таблица `table6`):**
- urban: Unintentional β>0 в **18/18** (ни один значим, медиана +0.025); Gardening β<0 в **18/18** (0 значимых); AgriForest β<0 в **18/18**, значим в **10/18**, медиана −0.312.
- cropland (проверка «не подмена ли это сельским хозяйством»): Unintentional β>0 в **18/18** (медиана +0.033) → **знак Unintentional не специфичен для urban**; AgriForest медиана всего −0.026, значим 2/18 → **отрицательная связь AgriForest urban-специфична**.

**6) Филогения в основной анализ НЕ включена.** Она неидентифицируема для этого вопроса. Опциональный appendix (77 видов, patristic PERMANOVA) выполнен и помечен как **другой вопрос**: pathway филогенетически кластеризован (pseudo-F=41.1, p=0.006) — про консерватиззм pathway, ничего не говорит про urban, в вывод не входит.

**Допуски не выбирались молча:** quasi-Poisson (φ=0.64–0.70, недо-дисперсия), NB2 (α=0.25 по profile-loglik) и HC1-робастный Пуассон дают **те же знаки и ту же картину значимости** (AgriForest p=.025 и p=.001; joint p=.013 и 1.4e-4); hurdle (binomial на 632 + состав на 191) меняет только вывод о **богатстве** (см. выше), но не о составе. Вывод от допущения не зависит.

**Глобальные проверки:** multinomial chi² pathway × терциль urban.2009.500m = 9.65, df=4, p=0.047 (min expected 6.46); PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis поComposition) p=0.154, стратифицированная по habitat p=0.128 — слабее и незначима (неadjusted, мало «эффективных» пар), поэтому как глобальный тест первичен GLM; псевдо-F здесь читают только против пермутационной базы (E[F]≈94.2 при случайном делении), абсолютное значение неинтерпретабельно.

## Ограничения
- Наблюдательные данные: все утверждения — ассоциации; в contingency таблицы городской переменной нет вообще, период = прокси эры.
- Pathway на уровне plot доступен только как counts (n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo), вид↔plot ключа нет → нельзя учесть видовой состав/филогению в urban-модели и нельзя отделить «одна популяция» от «много видов».
- 441/632 plot'ов пустые; AgriForest 23 records / 21 plot; низкая мощность для попарных сравнений.
- Причина роста доли Unintentional частично композиционная (сумма долей = 1); без внешнего (садового/торгового) слоя это неустранимо.
- Семантика `progressive/regressive` противоречит документации — вывод по знаку delta.
- Тренд «1956 → сильнее β по AgriForest» (β=−1.08 на 1000m) я интерпретировать причинно не могу: в данных нет ни годов интродукции на вид, ни исторического слоя сверх этих трёх лет.

Артефакты: исполняемый скрипт (один прогон, exit=0, воспроизводится с чистого каталога), 13 таблиц CSV + лог + текст гипотезы.

payload.answer:
Inspection pass done (no modelling). Findings + proposed approach below; awaiting your approval before running anything inferential.

## 1) Input inventory

| file | shape | delimiters/dtypes | missing | dup rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv | 12 x 3 | **tab**-delimited despite .csv; 2 str + int64 `n` | 0 | 0 |
| phylogenetic_tree.txt | 1 line Newick, 3.5 KB | 81 unique tips, branch lengths, internal labels are OpenTree `mrcaott*`, root label `Spermatophyta` | – | – |
| invasion_success_pathways.csv | 81 x 19 | comma; 9 numeric, 9 str, 1 bool | `genus.relative` 79/81 NA, `species.relative` 77/81 NA (effectively empty) | **0 exact duplicate rows** |
| invaded_niche_pathways.csv | **632 x 37** | **tab**-delimited; 36 numeric + 1 str (`habitat`) | 0 | 0 (632 unique lon/lat) |

Category levels:
- `introduction.period` (4, ordered): Before 1500 / 1501-1900 / 1901-1984 / 1985-2019. `pathway` (3): AgriForest, Gardening, Unintentional. Complete 4x3, N=1046. Period totals 107/121/290/528. Composition: AgriForest 51.4%→29.8→13.1→6.1%; Gardening 16.8→44.6→49.0→**75.2%**; Unintentional 31.8→25.6→37.9→18.8%.
- `intro.pathway` (3, same labels, no missings): Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9.
- `habitat` (10): Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29.

The `duplicated` flag: 4 TRUE, and these are **not** repeated rows — they are second lineages of conspecifics carrying a `2`-suffixed tip label (Eucalyptus_camaldulensis2, Opuntia_ficus-indica2, Oxalis_debilis2, Populus_deltoides2). 81 rows / 77 unique names. All 81 `phylo.tip.label` values match tree tips exactly (1:1), so the tree is usable if needed.

## 2) Urban / cropland coverage
Complete 2 x 3 x 3 factorial = **18 columns**: {urban, cropland} x {1956, 1993, 2009} x {50m, 500m, 1000m}. All numeric, no missings, values in **0–1 fractions** (metadata says "percentage" — rescale x100 when reporting).
Means (%, 2009): urban 11.1 / 13.1 / 13.2 at 50/500/1000 m; cropland 17.0 / 19.0 / 19.2. Cropland declines over time (34.9→19.0% @500m), urban triples (3.7→13.1% @500m).
Zero-inflation is the key constraint: urban 50 m is 87.5% zeros (1956) → 74.7% (2009); urban 500 m 47.5%→30.1%; 1000 m 37.2%→19.3%. Plots with urban.2009.500m ≥10%: **182 of 632**.

Change categories — **correction to the metadata**: the 6 columns `progressive/regressive/no.changes.{1956.2009,1993.2009}.50m` are **not binary categories**. They are continuous 0–1 proportions (75–100 distinct values each; means 0.22/0.18/0.58 and 0.16/0.13/0.70), and the triple sums to ~1 in 584/632 rows, i.e. share of the 50 m buffer area in each change state. They exist **only for the 50 m buffer**, and they are **not attributable to urban vs cropland**: plots whose dominant state is "progressive" actually lose cropland (Δ −0.32) and barely gain urban (+0.014), while "regressive" plots gain urban strongly (+0.33). I therefore treat them as a generic landscape-change index and **reconstruct urban change myself** from the year columns (urban increase 1956→2009: 134/389/458 plots at 50/500/1000 m).

Are the pathway columns usable as responses? Yes — per-plot **species counts**. Evidence: integer, ≥0, `n.total == n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo` in 632/632 rows; per-plot max 10 (≤81 species); plot sums (gard 169, unint 289, agfo 23, total 481) reconcile to within 2–5% with the species-table sums of `number.of.invaded.plots` by pathway (163/288/21, total 472). So each row = one plot, each cell = number of distinct invasive species of that pathway recorded in it. Sparsity: non-zero plots = 117 (gard), 145 (unint), **21 (agfo)**; 69.8% of plots have n.total = 0.

One descriptive (untested) signal so you can judge feasibility: mean counts rise monotonically across quintiles of urban.2009.500m — n.gard 0.05→0.61, n.unint 0.09→1.32, n.agfo 0.01→0.09. No inference run yet.

## 3) Proposed approach (not executed)
(a) **Context, not the answer**: chi-square + correspondence analysis on the 4x3 table (N=1046, df=6, min expected count 16.5 → Pearson chi-square valid) to establish that pathway composition shifted toward Gardening over time; report CA axes 1–2 and per-cell contributions.

(b) **Primary test** — plot-level, per pathway:
- Responses: `n.gard`, `n.unint`, `n.agfo` (separate models per pathway; `n.total` as secondary).
- Primary predictor: **urban cover 2009 at the 500 m buffer** (`urban.2009.500m`) — best compromise between local relevance and non-zero coverage (69.9% non-zero). 50 m and 1000 m reported as buffer sensitivity, not new hypotheses.
- Competing primary predictor: **urban increase** `urban.2009.500m − urban.1956.500m` (and 1993→2009 as a recency check). Never in the same model as the level: Spearman = 0.935.
- Models: GLM log-link; Poisson first, negative-binomial where dispersion warrants (VMR: gard 1.60, unint 2.35, agfo 1.14), plus a **hurdle / logistic presence–absence fit** because 77–82% of plots are zero. For `n.agfo` (21 non-zero plots) I would **not** fit a count model — logistic on presence/absence only, reported as exploratory.
- Covariates (all correlated with urban): elevation (ρ = −0.65), log distance.road (−0.56), annual temperature/rainfall. `habitat` as fixed factor in a sensitivity model only — the "Urban" habitat class is fully nested in cover > 0 (65/65), so it is partly redundant with the predictor.
- Contrasts: (i) identical models with `cropland.2009.500m`; (ii) formal slope comparison urban vs cropland (ρ = 0.24 between them, so a clean contrast); (iii) model-free Mann–Whitney of counts in urban (≥10% cover, n=182) vs non-urban (n=450) plots.
- Multiple comparisons: **Holm within the primary family of 6 tests** (3 pathways x {urban level, urban change}); buffers/years/cropland are declared sensitivity analyses, not extra families.
- Spatial non-independence: check residual Moran's I / variogram given coordinates; if autocorrelated, add distance-based eigenvector (PCNM) or habitat random effect.

**Primary designation**: responses = per-plot `n.gard` and `n.unint` counts (agfo secondary/exploratory); predictor set = urban 2009 cover at 500 m as the main axis, with reconstructed urban increase 1956→2009 as the rival primary axis, elevation + road distance + climate as covariates, cropland as contrast.

## 4) Assumptions and uncertainties
1. **n.\* semantics**: assumed species richness per plot per pathway (supported by the reconciliation above, but it is an inference; the 2–5% sum mismatch suggests a slightly different species/plot subset, and I cannot rule out repeat occurrences).
2. **Change-column semantics**: supplied progressive/regressive/no.changes are 50 m-only, continuous, and not urban-specific → I plan to reconstruct urban deltas. If you know the original classification's target class, that changes the predictor definition.
3. **Urban = current cover or urban increase?** Both are plausible readings of "influenced by urban land use". They are nearly collinear (ρ=0.94) so I would pick one per model and report both; the pathway most sensitive to *increase* (recent urbanisation) vs *current cover* may differ, which is itself an answer-relevant distinction.
4. **Collinearity** year x buffer (median ρ = 0.63, max 0.90) → one buffer+year per model; no all-in model.
5. **Confounding**: urban plots are lower, closer to roads, warmer/wetter → a pure urban effect must be separated from climate/elevation; habitat/urban redundancy also limits interpretation.
6. **Zero inflation / sparse agfo**: agfo has only 21 non-zero plots and 9 source species — likely underpowered; conclusions on AgriForest should be framed as weak.
7. **Scale mismatch**: contingency table is Catalonia-wide and species-level with introduction periods; plot table is Barcelona province with no temporal dimension — so (a) is context, and the plot analysis cannot itself date introductions. Linking them requires assuming pathway labels are the same classification in both files.
8. **Tree**: not needed for this question. It matters only if you want species-level phylogenetic robustness (PGLS/独立 contrasts on invasion success) — recommend excluding from the primary analysis, optionally as a sensitivity.
9. `duplicated`=TRUE rows: keep at species level (81 tips ↔ 81 labels) for any species-level work; irrelevant at plot level.
10. Deliverable caveat: no p-value can show *causality*; the output will be a data-grounded hypothesis, expected to centre on gardening (ornamental) introductions tracking urban cover, with unintentional as the comparison.

Artifacts: analysis/01_inspection.py (executed) and analysis/01_inspection_log.txt (full output).

¡Buenísimo! La inspección está impecable y el plan me convence; apruebo la fase de análisis. Solo fijo cuatro precisiones antes de que corras nada inferencial:

1) Eje primario: mantén `urban.2009.500m` como predictor principal, pero trata `urban.2009.500m - urban.1956.500m` como eje primario hermano, no como sensibilidad. Ambas lecturas de "uso de suelo urbano" son legítimas y la comparación nivel vs. incremento es parte de la respuesta. Nunca juntos en el mismo modelo (ρ=0.935, correcto).

2) Respuestas: `n.gard` y `n.unint` como modelos principales (Poisson → NB si la dispersión lo pide, más el ajuste hurdle/logístico por la inflación de ceros); `n.agfo` solo presencia/ausencia, etiquetado explícitamente como exploratorio y con potencia insuficiente; `n.total` secundario. Covariables: elevación, log distancia a carretera, temperatura y precipitación; `habitat` solo en un modelo de sensibilidad, documentando la redundancia de la clase "Urban". Cropland como contraste formal, con la comparación de pendientes urban vs. cropland reportada explícitamente.

3) Correcciones múltiples: Holm dentro de la familia primaria de 6 pruebas está bien; declara buffers, años, cropland y hábitat como sensibilidades declaradas a priori, no como familias nuevas. Revisa Moran's I sobre los residuos y, si hay autocorrelación, reporta el modelo con PCNM o con efecto aleatorio de hábitat como la versión conservadora.

4) Formato del entregable final: la hipótesis debe ser explícitamente data-grounded y nombrar las variables y las relaciones concretas (p. ej. vía de introducción × variable de cobertura urbana × buffer/año, dirección del efecto, tamaño del efecto con intervalo de confianza, y si la señal es por cobertura actual o por incremento histórico). Incluye también: (a) los resultados del chi-cuadrado/CA como contexto temporal, (b) una tabla resumen de coeficientes por vía para los modelos primarios y de sensibilidad, (c) las cifras descriptivas del gradiente por quintiles ya obtenidas, y (d) una sección de limitaciones que conserve tus advertencias sobre la semántica de `n.*`, la columnas progressive/regressive, la escala Cataluña vs. Barcelona y la potencia de AgriForest. El árbol filogenético queda fuera del análisis primario; si te da la gana, un PGLS de sensibilidad es opcional, no requerido.

Reporta números observados, no solo "significativo/no significativo". ¡Gracias por el trabajo tan prolijo! 🙌

El diseño primario responde a la pregunta: respuestas por vía (n.gard, n.unint) contra cobertura urbana y cambio urbano, con cropland como contraste, control de colinealidad (una combinación buffer/año por modelo), manejo de inflación de ceros, Holm en la familia primaria y chequeo de autocorrelación espacial. Las incertidumbres declaradas son honestas y acotadas; la única ambigüedad material (cobertura actual vs. incremento) queda resuelta manteniendo ambos como ejes primarios. Las correcciones a la metadata (fracciones 0-1, flag duplicated como linajes adicionales) son apropiadas. Solo quedan directrices de alcance y de formato del entregable, no una revisión estructural.

您好。请先只做资料核查与工作方案设计,暂不要给出最终结论或完整分析结果。

第一步(仅限核查):
1. 逐一读取 data/ 目录下的四个文件:temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv、invasion_success_pathways.csv、invaded_niche_pathways.csv、phylogenetic_tree.txt。
2. 报告每个文件的实际行数、列名(与数据集说明是否一致)、缺失值情况、类别变量的取值水平(尤其是 introduction.period 的时期分段、pathway / intro.pathway 的类别名称及拼写是否一致)。
3. 说明 temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv 中 introduction.period 与 pathway 的交叉表结构,以及 n 的合计是否可用于时序趋势判断。
4. 说明 invaded_niche_pathways.csv 中各 urban.* 与 cropland.*(50m/500m/1000m,1956/1993/2009)及 progressive/regressive/no.changes 变量的可用性、单位与缺失情况。
5. 确认 invasion_success_pathways.csv 中 intro.pathway 与途径计数列(n.gard、n.unint、n.agfo)能否彼此对应,以及 phylogenetic_tree.txt 的叶标签与 phylo.tip.label 是否可匹配(仅报告匹配率,不做系统发育分析)。

第二步(仅提出方案,勿执行完整分析):
请提出一个针对研究问题「哪些类型的植物引入途径受到了城市土地利用的影响」的分析方案,至少包含:
- 以何种统计量衡量途径构成随时期(以及随城市用地比例/城市用地变化)的变化,例如卡方适合度检验或广义对应分析、逻辑回归;
- 以哪些城市土地利用变量作为主要解释变量(尺度 50m/500m/1000m、年份、渐进/退化变化),以及为何选定该尺度;
- 如何处理多途径同时存在、零计数、以及物种非独立性问题(是否暂不纳入系统发育部分)。

同时请明确列出您的关键假设与不确定之处,例如:时期与年份的对应关系是否可比、途径标签的映射假设、把城市用地百分比当作解释变量而非结果变量的因果方向假设。请区分「数据中确证的事实」与「您的推断假设」。完成后先返回核查报告与方案,等待我的确认。

payload.message:
Thanks. Before any modelling, please do a read-only inspection pass and report back — do not run the full analysis yet.

1) Inventory the four supplied files (data/temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv, data/invasion_success_pathways.csv, data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv, data/phylogenetic_tree.txt): shapes, key columns, factor levels of `intro.pathway` / `pathway`, row units (species vs. plot/habitat × pathway counts), missingness, duplicates flag, and whether species labels in invasion_success_pathways.csv match `phylo.tip.label` and Newick tip labels.

2) Confirm which variables actually operationalise "urban land use": the urban.* buffers at 50/500/1000 m for 1956/1993/2009, plus the progressive/regressive/no.changes landscape-change categories, and whether cropland and urban are both present at each buffer so we can separate urbanisation from agricultural change.

3) Propose a concrete, minimal analysis plan that answers "what types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?", i.e. which introduction pathways (Gardening / AgriForest / Unintentional) track urban cover or urbanisation. I suggest the plan cover (a) pathway-specific responses to urban % at the three buffers and three dates (e.g. GLMs/GLMMs or pathway-count multinomial/DIRichlet-style composition models on the pathway counts n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo with habitat as a blocking factor), (b) the temporal contingency table as a descriptive complement (chi-square / correspondence analysis of pathway × period, with the urban-expansion timeline as interpretive context), and (c) a check for collinearity among urban/cropland/distance.road/elevation/climate covariates so pathway effects are not confounded.

4) State explicitly your assumptions and any consequential uncertainties: whether invaded_niche_pathways.csv rows are plots (so pathway columns are counts per plot, not species-level traits), whether the temporal trends file is sufficient to infer causality or only association, and whether the phylogeny is needed at all for this question (I lean toward treating it as optional, e.g. a phylogenetically corrected sensitivity check only if pathway signal is strong).

Return the inspection summary, the proposed approach, and the assumption list. Hold off on final inference until we agree on the approach.

payload.answer:
READ-ONLY INSPECTION + PROPOSED APPROVAL-GATED PLAN (no modelling run yet)

===================================================
1) INVENTORY OF THE FOUR FILES
===================================================
A. data/temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv — 12 rows x 3 cols (tab-separated, quoted). Columns: introduction.period (4 ordered levels: Before 1500, 1501-1900, 1901-1984, 1985-2019), pathway (3: AgriForest, Gardening, Unintentional), n (int). Perfectly balanced 4x3, 0 missing, 0 duplicates, total N = 1046 species-records (NOT 632 plots and NOT the 81 species — this is the full Catalan naturalised flora).
   n:  AgriForest 55/36/38/32 (flat); Gardening 18/54/142/397; Unintentional 34/31/110/99.
   Within-period Gardening share 0.17 -> 0.45 -> 0.49 -> 0.75; AgriForest share 0.51 -> 0.30 -> 0.13 -> 0.06.
   Descriptive check only: chi2 = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6.3e-47 (min expected cell 16.5, so chi2 is valid). Std residuals: 1985-2019 Gardening +5.0, AgriForest -5.5, Unintentional -3.3; Before 1500 AgriForest +9.5, Gardening -5.6. Hand-computed CA: axis 1 holds 88.3% of inertia and orders periods Before1500 (-1.06) -> 1985-2019 (+0.34), with AgriForest (-0.91) vs Gardening (+0.32) at the ends; axis 2 separates Unintentional.

B. data/invasion_success_pathways.csv — 81 rows x 19 cols (COMMA-separated; note different delimiter). Unit = species (with 4 replicated rows): 77 unique Scientific_name, 0 exact duplicate rows, and a 'duplicated' flag TRUE for exactly 4 rows (Eucalyptus_camaldulensis2, Opuntia_ficus-indica2, Oxalis_debilis2, Populus_deltoides2) — i.e. the extra rows are conspecific second records distinguished only by the "2" suffix on the tip label. Only missing values: genus.relative (79 NA) and species.relative (77 NA) — effectively empty. intro.pathway levels: Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9 (42/30/9 include duplicates; on 77 unique rows: 50.6% / 37.7% / 11.7%). Other factors: family (33 levels), growth.form (Perennial fg 30 / Shrub-tree 27 / Annual fg 24), dispersal (Unspecific 42 / Animal 21 / Wind 18), vegetative (No 46 / Yes 35).
   Pathway means (useful context): number.of.invaded.plots Unintentional 9.6 > Gardening 3.9 > AgriForest 2.3; mrt ~86-106 yr. So the two files disagree in pathway emphasis (species file is Gardening-heavy; plot records are Unintentional-heavy) — see assumption A4.

C. data/phylogenetic_tree.txt — single-line Newick, fully parsed with a recursive-descent parser: 81 tips, 20 labelled internal nodes (mrcaott* OpenTree labels + one 'Caryophyllales.rn.d8s.tre'), all tips carry branch lengths.
   TIP MATCH: set(tree tips) == set(invasion_success_pathways.phylo.tip.label) EXACTLY (81/81, zero mismatches either direction). phylo.tip.label is NOT genus+"_"+species (the 'species' column actually holds the binomial); it is the binomial with spaces->underscores plus a trailing "2" for the 4 duplicated rows. So phylogeny joins cleanly to the species file only.

D. data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv — 632 rows x 37 cols (TAB-separated). 0 missing, 0 duplicate rows, 632 unique (longitude, latitude) pairs -> one row = one plot, no plot ID column. habitat = 10 levels (Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29).
   n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo == n.total in 100% of rows. Totals over plots: gard 169, unint 289, agfo 23, total 481. Heavily zero-inflated: 441/632 plots (70%) have n.total = 0; zeros per column gard 515, unint 487, agfo 611. Variance/mean: gard 1.6, unint 2.35, agfo 1.14. Max n.total = 10 (gard 4, unint 7, agfo 2).
   Signal is concentrated: plots with >=1 species by habitat = Urban 54/65, Croplands 51/92, Riparian 32/61, Wetlands 21/38, Coastal 16/29, and <=5 for the five remaining (forests/meadows/scrub/rock) habitats. Excluding Urban-habitat plots leaves 567 plots / 330 records (gard 124, unint 185, agfo 21).
   NOTE: max number.of.invaded.plots in the species file is 53 and its sum is 472 (481 plot-records) — the two files are consistent in magnitude but do not reconcile exactly, so the plot file cannot be reproduced from the 81 species alone.

===================================================
2) WHAT ACTUALLY OPERATIONALISES "URBAN LAND USE"
===================================================
- 9 urban.* layers = 3 dates (1956, 1993, 2009) x 3 buffers (50/500/1000 m); cropland.* has the IDENTICAL 9-layer grid, so urbanisation and agricultural change can be separated. Values are PROPORTIONS 0-1, not percentages, despite the "percentage" wording in datasets.json.
- Urban is sparse and increasing: mean 0.040 -> 0.082 -> 0.111 (50 m) and 0.034 -> 0.090 -> 0.132 (1000 m); frac>0 rises 0.13 -> 0.25 (50 m), 0.63 -> 0.81 (1000 m). Cropland DECLINES over the same window: 0.308 -> 0.170 (50 m), 0.353 -> 0.192 (1000 m); cropland decreased 1956->2009 in 43% of plots at 50 m. So urban gain and cropland loss are temporally anti-coincident region-wide (rural abandonment + urban growth), which is good for identification.
- Landscape-change categories exist ONLY at the 50 m buffer, only for two windows (1956-2009 and 1993-2009), and are proportions (0-1), not factor labels: progressive / regressive / no.changes. The triples do NOT sum exactly to 1 (mean 0.982/0.989; exactly 1 in only ~80% of rows; min 0.44), so they are best treated as three continuous composition covariates rather than a single factor.
- IMPORTANT semantic caveat: these categories do not track urban change the way the metadata suggests. Spearman(progressive_1956-2009_50m, urban delta) = -0.16 and with cropland delta = -0.39, while Spearman(regressive, urban delta) = +0.48. Interpretation: "progressive/regressive" appears to describe change in the natural/non-urban host cover (or is coded oppositely to the documentation). I will treat urban.<date>.<buffer> (and its derived delta) as the primary urbanisation variables and the progressive/regressive set as a secondary, exploratory predictor with this caveat stated.
- A separate categorical 'Urban' HABITAT class (65 plots, median urban.2009.50m = 0.95) also exists; it is a sampling stratum, not a land-use predictor, and it overlaps but is not identical to high urban cover (46/65 have urban.50m > 0.5).
- Additional plot covariates: elevation, distance.stream, distance.road, longitude/latitude (UTM metres), annual.temperature / rainfall / radiation.

===================================================
3) PROPOSED MINIMAL ANALYSIS PLAN (agree before I run it)
===================================================
Primary inferential unit = plot (invaded_niche_pathways.csv). Question re-cast as: does the pathway composition of established non-native species at a plot vary with urban cover, or with urban gain, holding cropland and environment constant?

(a) Pathway-specific responses to urban cover / urbanisation
  A0. Predictor set (one urban layer per model to avoid VIF blow-up): primary = urban.2009.1000m (best filled: 81% plots >0, mean 0.13), plus buffer/date sensitivity across all 9 layers, plus delta_urban_1956_2009 at 500/1000 m, plus exploratory progressive/regressive (50 m only). Controls: cropland (same year+buffer), elevation, distance.road, and coarse habitat block. All predictors centred/scaled.
  A1. COMPOSITION (headline model): Dirichlet-multinomial / multinomial logit on (n.gard, n.unint, n.agfo) with n.total as the number of trials, fitted on the 191 plots with n.total > 0. Gives directly interpretable "share of introductions per pathway vs urban %". Because AgriForest has only 23 records overall, I will ALSO fit the 2-way Gardening vs Unintentional contrast (binomial) as the well-powered version of the same question.
  A2. PATHWAY-SPECIFIC ABUNDANCE: quasi-Poisson / negative-binomial GLM per pathway (n.gard, n.unint, n.agfo ~ urban + cropland + elevation + distance.road + habitat block), plus a hurdle view (binomial on presence/absence of each pathway) since 70% of plots are species-free. This separates "more invaders in urban plots" from "a different mix of pathways".
  A3. BLOCKING: habitat enters as a fixed block, collapsed to 4 groups that actually carry records (Urban; Croplands; Riparian+Wetlands+Coastal; Dry-upland = forests/meadows/scrub/rock), because 10 free levels against 191 informative plots and a 23-record AgriForest cell would be over-parameterised. I will report the full 10-level version as a check.
  A4. Model selection / multiplicity: pre-register urban.2009.1000m + composition model as primary; the other 8 layers and the delta/change variants are a family compared by AICc with Holm correction across the family, so the reported effect is not buffer-shopping.
  A5. Sensitivity: (i) drop the 65 Urban-habitat plots (567 plots remain, still 330 records incl. 124 gardening) to prove the signal is not just "urban plots have more species"; (ii) drop cropland-habitat plots; (iii) with/without climate; (iv) spatial autocorrelation check on residuals (plot coordinates are available).

(b) Temporal contingency table as descriptive complement
  Chi-square on the 4x3 table (chi2 = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6e-47 already verified valid), standardised residual decomposition, and 2-D correspondence analysis (axis 1 = 88% of inertia, AgriForest->Gardening gradient ordered in time). Reported as association over introduction periods, with the Barcelona urban-expansion timeline (urban cover roughly tripled 1956->2009; cropland halved) used as interpretive context only. Explicit caveat: the period bins (Before 1500 / 1501-1900 / 1901-1984 / 1985-2019) do not align with the land-cover dates (1956/1993/2009), so the temporal file can motivate but cannot test an urban link; also introduction-period counts are right-censored (recent species have had less time to be recorded/establish).

(c) Collinearity screen (so pathway effects are not confounded)
  Already computed: urban layers are mutually r <= 0.90 (500m-1000m same date) -> one layer per model. Urban vs cropland at the SAME buffer/date is only weakly correlated (50 m: |rho| <= 0.08; 1000 m: 0.24-0.26 in 1993/2009, 0.63 in 1956), so urban and cropland are separable in the models — good news for the question. Elevation vs annual.temperature rho = -0.96 -> keep one (elevation primary, temperature as sensitivity). Full-set VIFs exceed 10 for urban.500m/1000m (13.8/11.8), elevation (13.1), temperature (21.8), rainfall (10.4), confirming the one-urban-layer + one-terrain/climate-variable rule. Also habitat class alone explains R2 = 0.47 of urban.2009.1000m and 0.55 of urban.2009.50m, hence the explicit Urban-habitat-exclusion sensitivity in A5(i).

(d) Phylogeny: OPTIONAL, deferred (I agree with your lean). It joins only the 81-species file, which carries no plot-level urban covariates, so it cannot inform the urban question directly. Fallback if the composition signal is strong: PGLS / phylogenetic ANOVA on species-level number.of.invaded.plots (or pathway-weighted means) to show the pathway pattern is not driven by a single clade (Asteraceae = 14/81 species).

Deliverable: a data-grounded hypothesis statement + the executed script (composition GLM, per-pathway GLMs, contingency/CA, collinearity diagnostics, sensitivity table).

===================================================
4) ASSUMPTIONS & UNCERTAINTIES (please confirm/overrule)
===================================================
A1. invaded_niche_pathways.csv rows = individual plots (632 unique coordinates, no ID). n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo are counts of pathway-assigned species recorded per plot, i.e. species x plot incidences, NOT species-level traits and NOT independent observations. Consequence: species identity is lost in this file, so no species random effect and no phylogenetic correction are possible here; and the 81 species are each counted up to 53 times, which inflates apparent sample size — I will treat overdispersion explicitly (quasi-Poisson/NB or Dirichlet-multinomial) rather than plain Poisson.
A2. urban.* and cropland.* are proportions 0-1 (max exactly 1.0), contrary to the "percentage" description. I will multiply by 100 for reporting and say so.
A3. The temporal file is a summary of the whole Catalan naturalised flora (1046 records), not of these 632 plots or 81 species. It supports association only: no causal claim (introduction period is confounded with propagule pressure, trade globalisation, recording effort, and time-since-introduction; and period bins do not match the 1956/1993/2009 land-cover dates).
A4. Pathway assignment is treated as a fixed species-level attribute, identical across the three files (levels match exactly: Gardening / AgriForest / Unintentional). The three files have different pathway compositions (species 0.51/0.12/0.38 gard/agfo/unint; plot records 0.35/0.05/0.60; temporal file 0.58/0.15/0.26) — expected because they cover different species pools and weight species by occupancy, but it means cross-file consistency checks are qualitative, not numeric. The 472 (species file) vs 481 (plot file) record totals do not reconcile; I assume the plot file draws on a slightly larger species list than the 81-species success table.
A5. progressive/regressive/no.changes semantics are only partially trusted (correlations above); urban.<date>.<buffer> is the primary urbanisation measure. If you know the coding convention from the source paper, that would remove this uncertainty.
A6. AgriForest is near-uninformable at plot level (23 records, 611 zero plots, max 2 per plot). Expect wide/possibly non-estimable AgriForest coefficients; conclusions for AgriForest will be framed as "no detectable urban association, low power", not as a null finding.
A7. The strongest a-priori confound: habitat/plot selection. Urban plots are sampled in the Urban habitat stratum, which is also where invaders concentrate. The Urban-habitat-exclusion run (A5-i) is the decisive test that any reported pattern is a land-use gradient and not a sampling-stratum artefact.
A8. No spatial random effect/coordinate-based blocking in the primary model (only 191 informative plots); residual spatial autocorrelation is checked as a sensitivity. Coordinate values are UTM metres (lon ~415000, lat ~4620000), not degrees.
A9. Python environment has pandas/numpy/scipy/statsmodels only — no ete3/Bio/dendropy, so any phylogenetic step would need a hand-rolled parsimony-free approach (e.g. cophenetic distance from my own Newick parser) or a package install; another reason to keep (d) optional.

OPEN DECISIONS I NEED FROM YOU: (i) accept habitat collapsed to 4 blocks as primary with 10-level as check? (ii) accept urban.2009.1000m as the pre-registered primary layer with 500 m / delta-urban as secondary? (iii) restrict composition modelling to n.total > 0 plots (my recommendation) or keep all 632 with a hurdle structure? (iv) confirm phylogeny stays optional.

payload.message:
Plan approved — this is a well-scoped, honest approach. Proceed with the main analysis. Answers to your four open decisions, plus a few binding constraints on how results get reported.

DECISIONS
(i) Habitat: YES — collapsed 4 blocks (Urban; Croplands; Riparian+Wetlands+Coastal; Dry-upland) as primary, full 10-level as a robustness check. With 191 informative plots and 23 AgriForest records, 10 free levels is over-parameterised. Report both coefficient tables so the collapse is auditable, and confirm the 4-block grouping is not itself drawn on the pathway data (define it a priori from habitat semantics, as you have).
(ii) Urban layer: YES — pre-register urban.2009.1000m as the primary urbanisation predictor, with delta_urban (1956→2009 at 500/1000 m) as the key secondary test, and the remaining layers as an AICc family under Holm. Please present the full 9-layer × 3-response effect grid in a supplementary table rather than narrating each one, so it is visibly not buffer-shopping. I agree with your reading of progressive/regressive: keep them exploratory only, and do not headline them given the semantic contradiction you found (regressive correlating +0.48 with urban delta). Flag that contradiction explicitly in the write-up as a documented data/coding inconsistency.
(iii) Plots with n.total > 0: YES — restrict the composition model to the 191 plots, and additionally fit the hurdle presence/absence view on all 632 plots (presence of each pathway) exactly as you proposed. The hurdle view is what lets us say whether urban plots host more invaders versus a different pathway mix, and I want both reported, not just the composition model.
(iv) Phylogeny: YES — stays optional/deferred. Only run it if the composition signal survives A5(i). If you do run it, a hand-rolled cophenetic distance from your own Newick parser plus PGLS/phylogenetic ANOVA on number.of.invaded.plots is sufficient; do not burn effort building a tree pipeline, and do not install packages if unavailable — a documented skip is acceptable.

BINDING REPORTING CONSTRAINTS
1. AgriForest: per your A6, report it as "no detectable urban association, low power" with the confidence interval shown, never as a null result. Do not let the headline hypothesis rest on an AgriForest coefficient.
2. The decisive test is A5(i), excluding the 65 Urban-habitat plots (567 plots, 330 records, 124 gardening). Since habitat alone explains 47–55% of urban-cover variance, the final hypothesis must be qualified by whether the pathway–urban association survives that exclusion. Please make that run a first-class result, not a footnote, and state the comparison of the primary vs Urban-excluded Gardening-vs-Unintentional coefficient directly.
3. Separation of urban from cropland is the crux of "urban land use" specifically: keep the same-buffer/same-date cropland term in every primary model, and report urban and cropland coefficients side by side. Your finding that they are only weakly collinear at the same buffer/date is the main reason this question is answerable at all, so make it visible.
4. Direction of causality: frame the deliverable as an association hypothesis (urban cover and urban gain are associated with a shift in the pathway composition of established non-native flora toward gardening/ornamental introductions and away from agroforestry, with unintentional introductions tracking [result]), and name the plausible mechanisms (ornamental garden escape as a local source; propagule pressure and trade globalisation; disturbance/substrate availability in urban plots) as mechanisms, not established findings.
5. Use the temporal contingency table and CA strictly as descriptive context — chi-square plus standardised residuals plus the 2-D CA — with the two caveats you already identified (period bins do not align with the 1956/1993/2009 land-cover dates; recent periods right-censored by establishment and recording lag). Do not let the strong chi-square (230.4, df 6) do causal work.
6. Report the overdispersion treatment explicitly (quasi-Poisson/NB dispersion parameter or Dirichlet-multinomial concentration) and the residual spatial-autocorrelation check, given species are counted up to 53 times.

DELIVERABLE
Return the final submission in the required contract form: a natural-language hypothesis in `answer` (and mirrored in payload.hypothesis), a concise `workflow` description of the executed models and their order, and the analysis artifacts (script(s), and a results/summary output including the collinearity diagnostics, the primary + Urban-excluded comparison, the 9-layer sensitivity grid, and the contingency/CA output). Keep the hypothesis explicit about which pathways increase, decrease, or are uninformative under urban cover/urban gain, at which buffer, and with which covariates held constant — the variable and relation detail matters as much as the narrative.

One clarification that would remove your A5 uncertainty, if you can find it in the data rather than from me: test whether progressive/regressive are better explained as change in natural/non-urban host cover by correlating them against the cropland delta and the implied residual (1 − urban − cropland) cover change. If that resolves it, you may promote the change categories to a legitimate secondary predictor; if not, leave them exploratory. No external study knowledge is required or assumed here.

payload.answer:
READ-ONLY INSPECTION PASS — complete, no modelling performed. All numbers below come from an executed script (`inspection/inspect_data_readonly.py`, full output in `inspection/inspection_report.txt`, 310 lines).

## 0. First, three file-format gotchas (they change everything downstream)
- `temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv` and `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` are **TAB-delimited** (despite the .csv extension); `invasion_success_pathways.csv` is comma-delimited. Reading the first two with the default comma separator silently yields 1 column.
- `longitude`/`latitude` in the plot file are **not degrees**: they are projected metres (E 368645–481175, N 4562825–4684875; extent 113 × 122 km, consistent with a UTM-like zone for Barcelona). Good news: distances in metres are directly usable in spatial models.
- The metadata's unit wording ("percentage") is **wrong** — see §3.

## 1. Shapes, levels, missingness
| file | rows × cols | NA |
|---|---|---|
| temporal_trends_contingency_table | 12 × 3 (4 periods × 3 pathways) | 0 |
| invasion_success_pathways | 81 × 19 | 156 (all in `genus.relative` 79/81 NA, `species.relative` 77/81 NA) |
| invaded_niche_pathways | 632 × 37 | **0 in every column** |
| phylogenetic_tree.txt | 1 Newick string: 81 tips, 19 labelled internal nodes, 158 branch lengths (0.12–325) | – |

Levels (species table after de-duplication, n = 77):
- `intro.pathway` (3): Gardening 39, Unintentional 29, AgriForest **9**
- `growth.form` (3): Perennial fg 29, Shrub/tree 24, Annual fg 24
- `dispersal` (3): Unspecific 40, Animal 20, Wind 17
- `vegetative` (2): No 45, Yes 32
- `family`: 33 families (Asteraceae 14, Poaceae 10, Amaranthaceae 7)
Contingency table uses the same 3 pathway labels; periods: "Before 1500", "1501-1900", "1901-1984", "1985-2019".

Plot-file `habitat` (10 levels, complete): Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29.

**Change classes are NOT categories.** `progressive/regressive/no.changes.*` are continuous 0–1 fractions (91, 86, 100 distinct values per column) that nearly sum to 1 row-wise (mean 0.982/0.989; 56 and 52 rows deviate by >0.01; min row-sum 0.00 and 0.44). They exist only for the 50 m buffer, for 1956→2009 and 1993→2009. So they are a compositional landscape-change typology, and the metadata never says whether "progressive" means urban, cropland, or either.

## 2. `genus.relative` / `species.relative` are near-useless
`genus.relative` has 2 values (a taxonomic synonym: *Jarava plumosa*→*Calamagrostis*, *Rumex cristatus*→*Rheum*); `species.relative` is populated **only** on the 4 `duplicated==TRUE` rows and just repeats the species name (a cross-reference key). Drop both.

## 3. Unit/scale of urban.* and cropland.*
All 18 columns are **0–1 fractions**, never > 1 (max 1.000), and `urban + cropland ≤ 1.000` in every row/year/buffer → proportions of one land-cover total. Examples (n = 632): urban.1956.50m mean 0.040 (553 zeros), urban.2009.50m 0.111 (472 zeros), urban.2009.500m 0.131, urban.2009.1000m 0.132; cropland declines 1956→2009 (0.308→0.170 at 50 m; 0.353→0.192 at 1000 m) while urban rises (0.040→0.111 at 50 m; 0.034→0.132 at 1000 m). Multiply by 100 for percentages; the dictionary wording is incorrect.

## 4. Analysis unit of invaded_niche_pathways
**One row per plot** (632 unique lat/lon pairs, no repeats; no plot ID needed) — *not* plot × pathway. `n.gard`, `n.unint`, `n.agfo` are species counts of that pathway in that plot and sum exactly to `n.total` in all 632 rows. Richness is sparse/zero-inflated: n.gard 81.5 % zeros (max 4), n.unint 77.1 % (max 7), n.agfo **96.7 %** (max 2), n.total 69.8 % zeros (max 10, var/mean 2.9). Only **191 / 632 plots are invaded**. Coordinates present in 632/632 rows.
Reconciliation with the species table **fails by design**: Σ`number.of.invaded.plots` = 472 (all 81 rows) or 452 (de-duplicated) vs Σ`n.total` = 481; per pathway AgriForest 21 vs 23, Gardening 155/163 vs 169, Unintentional 276/289. Interpretation: the plot file summarises a **larger invaded flora / plot network** than the 77-species trait table, i.e. the trait table is a trait-complete subset. Consequence: **no species × plot incidence matrix exists**, and one cannot be rebuilt. The 1046 species in the contingency table are Catalonia-wide introductions — a third, larger universe.

## 5. Duplicated flag and tree tips — both clean
`duplicated==TRUE` on exactly 4 rows (*Eucalyptus camaldulensis*, *Opuntia ficus-indica*, *Oxalis debilis*, *Populus deltoides*); each is a **dual-pathway species listed twice with a different `intro.pathway`**, all other columns identical. Dropping them gives **77 rows = 77 unique species = one row per species**. Tree: exactly **81 tips and all 81 `phylo.tip.label` values match** (the 4 duplicates get their own tip with a trailing `2`, e.g. `Oxalis_debilis2`); no tree tip is unused. Matching requires hyphens in the label regex (`Opuntia_ficus-indica`) or you get 2 spurious misses.

## 6. Collinearity (correlations only — nothing fitted)
Within-urban across year × buffer (Pearson): 0.56–0.96. Worst pairs are same-year/adjacent-buffer (500 m vs 1000 m: 0.96 in 1956, 0.95 in 1993, **0.95 in 2009**) and same-buffer/adjacent-era (1993 vs 2009: 0.84 at 50 m, 0.92 at 500 m, 0.95 at 1000 m). Every urban column has max |r| ≥ 0.84 with another land-cover column.
**urban vs cropland is nearly orthogonal**: contemporaneous |r| ≤ 0.15; only cross-era pairs reach 0.36–0.43 (urban.2009.1000m vs cropland.1956.1000m). So collinearity is a *within-class* problem (years/buffers), not urban-vs-cropland — cropland can stay as an independent covariate.
The real confounder is environment/climate: urban.2009.1000m vs elevation r = −0.53, annual.temperature +0.51, rainfall −0.35, distance.road −0.26; `habitat=="Urban"` vs urban.2009.1000m r = 0.60 (a habitat term therefore partly absorbs the predictor of interest).
Descriptive (no model): mean richness by quartile of urban.2009.1000m → total 0.12, 0.43, 0.73, **1.93**; unintentional 0.06→**1.24**, gardening 0.05→**0.62**, agri-forestry 0.009→0.064; % invaded plots 7.5→70.7. Cropland quartiles give a much weaker gradient (0.53→1.03). Plots whose 50 m urban cover increased 1956→2009: mean 1.66 vs stable 0.48. Median splits show urban lifts unintentional richness even in low-cropland plots (0.05→0.76). Species-level descriptive: mean invaded plots Unintentional 9.5 vs Gardening 4.0 vs AgriForest 2.3; Wind 9.9 vs Unspecific 5.0 / Animal 4.3; Annual fg 10.6 vs Perennial 4.3 vs Shrub/tree 3.0.

## 7. Proposed approach for "how did urban land use affect the invasion of different types of introduced plants?"
**Response (primary): pathway-specific species richness per plot** (`n.gard`, `n.unint`, `n.agfo`), Poisson/negative-binomial GLMM. It is the only response that can actually be regressed on urban land use, because urban varies **only among plots**; and richness beats presence/absence (the binary version discards gradient information and gives the same sign). Species-level occupancy (`number.of.invaded.plots`, `area.of.occupancy.10km`) is **not** regressible on plot urban cover (no species × plot link) and gets a secondary, non-causal role (§8).
**Lead predictor: `urban.2009.500m`**, with `cropland.2009.500m` kept as a separate covariate. Why: (i) 50 m is unusable as a continuous slope (75 % zeros in 2009 — effectively a 3-level variable); (ii) 500 m and 1000 m are r = 0.95, so 500 m carries the same information at a scale closer to the propagule-pressure/disturbance story and less confounded with regional climate/elevation; (iii) 2009 is the layer contemporaneous with the survey. Sensitivity set: swap buffer (50 m / 1000 m), swap year (1956, 1993) to test **legacy vs contemporaneous** urbanisation, and PCA1 of the nine urban columns as a scale-free version. One year × buffer per model — never 1993.1000m together with 2009.1000m.
**"Types of introduced plants"**: lead contrast = `intro.pathway`, estimated **as an urban × type interaction** by stacking the plot file into long format (632 × 3 = 1896 rows, count = n.<pathway>, plus pathway fixed effect), so the interaction *is* the answer to "different types". Secondary contrasts: growth.form, dispersal, vegetative (same machinery). AgriForest needs a decision (uncertainty 1).
**Confounders**: elevation, annual.temperature, annual.rainfall, distance.road, distance.stream; habitat as a *sensitivity* analysis rather than baseline, because `habitat=="Urban"` correlates 0.60 with the predictor.
**Spatial autocorrelation**: median nearest-neighbour 1316 m over 113 × 122 km → spatial random field on the projected coordinates (Matérn GP or spatial eigenvector mapping), reporting Moran's I on residuals before/after.
**Zero inflation**: n.agfo 96.7 %, n.gard 81.5 % zeros → NB2 with observation-level random effect; if AgriForest is retained, a two-part (presence then count) model.

## 8. Do the phylogeny and the contingency table earn a place?
**Contingency table: no — background framing only.** No plot, no urban measure, different universe (1046 Catalonia-wide introductions vs 77 trait-complete invaded species in 632 Barcelona plots). Its legitimate use is context: pathway composition shifted strongly (χ² = 230.4, df 6, Cramér's V = 0.332), Gardening rising from 2.9 % of introductions before 1500 to 65.0 % in 1985–2019 while AgriForest fell 34.2 %→19.9 %. It motivates the hypothesis; it cannot test it.
**Phylogeny: partial — secondary only.** It cannot contribute to the urban effect (species are never linked to plots) and n = 77 tips across 33 families buys little. One bounded use: PGLS of `number.of.invaded.plots` (or AOO) on pathway + growth form + dispersal + height + mrt, using the 81-tip tree with the 4 dual-pathway tips collapsed onto their species, to check the trait/pathway signal is not a phylogenetic artefact. A leaner answer can drop the tree entirely and I will say so.

## 9. Assumptions (as assumptions, not facts)
1. `n.*` are species richness per pathway per plot, and the vegetation survey is contemporaneous with the 2009 land-cover layer.
2. Coordinates are a UTM-like projected CRS in metres (magnitudes fit; EPSG undocumented).
3. Urban cover proxies propagule pressure + disturbed substrate; neither is measured directly.
4. `number.of.invaded.plots` refers to the same plot network as the 632 rows (the 29-incidence mismatch suggests it partly does not).
5. Pathway-specific counts within a plot are conditionally independent given covariates — violated if dual-pathway species co-occur, hence the pathway-marginal stacked design.

## 10. Genuinely open choices — your call before I fit anything
1. **AgriForest**: 9 species / 23 plot incidences / 96.7 % zeros — estimate as-is (huge CI), pool with Unintentional, or contrast only Gardening vs Unintentional? My default: keep, report as uninformative.
2. **Habitat**: covariate, stratifier, or omitted (r = 0.60 with the predictor). My default: omit from baseline, report as sensitivity.
3. **Headline urban year**: contemporaneous 2009 vs legacy 1956/1993 vs the `progressive` change fraction. Caveat: no invasion *year* per plot exists (only species-level `mrt`), so no year is strictly "correct" and inference stays associational.
4. **Response form**: stacked long model with urban × pathway interaction (my default) vs three separate per-pathway models (readable, no formal interaction test).
5. **Spatial structure**: full GP/Matérn (my default — `mgcv`/`brms` availability not yet verified) vs Moran's-I-then-eigenvectors vs none.
6. **Phylogeny in or out** of the final answer, and whether the 4 dual-pathway species are dropped (my default) or counted in both pathways.
7. **Deliverable framing**: quantitative effect size (e.g. "% more unintentional species per doubling of urban cover") vs a ranked qualitative hypothesis.

No model has been fitted. If you approve §7 with your calls on §10, I will run the stacked pathway-interaction GLMMs, the buffer/year sensitivity set, the Moran's-I diagnostics, and (if you want) the PGLS check, then write the final natural-language hypothesis.

Plan approved — this is a good inspection pass and §7 is the right shape. Proceed to fitting. Here are my calls on §10, plus three things I want added.

MY CALLS
1. AgriForest: restrict the formal interaction test to Gardening vs Unintentional. Report AgriForest descriptively (counts, quartile gradient, crude model with CI if it converges) and label it uninformative. Do not pool it with Unintentional — that would silently redefine the pathway contrast, which is the deliverable.
2. Habitat: omit from baseline, report as sensitivity (your default). Additionally run one sensitivity model that EXCLUDES the 65 habitat=="Urban" plots entirely, because recording invaders in plots classified as urban habitat while regressing on urban land cover is partly circular. I want the urban coefficient with and without those plots.
3. Headline predictor: urban.2009.500m, with urban.1956.500m and urban.1993.500m as the legacy sensitivity, and say explicitly which fits better. Keep progressive.1956.2009.50m as a secondary predictor only, framed as "land-cover change in the 50 m buffer (direction undocumented)".
4. Response form: stacked long model with the urban × pathway interaction as the primary result, AND the three separate per-pathway coefficients in a table. Both, not one.
5. Spatial structure: first verify what is actually installed (mgcv/brms/ape/PyMC). If a GP is unavailable, fall back to a Moran's-I screen plus spatial eigenvectors/PCNM and say which you used. Do not stall on a missing package.
6. Phylogeny: keep as a bounded secondary PGLS on number.of.invaded.plots with the 4 dual-pathway tips collapsed. For the plot-level stacked analysis, keep dual-pathway species counted in both pathways — that is what n.gard/n.unint already encode; dropping them there would mismatch the plot sums. If ape/PGLS is unavailable, state that plainly and set the tree aside rather than inventing a substitute.
7. Deliverable: both — a quantitative effect size (e.g. % change in unintentional richness per doubling of urban cover, with CI) AND a short ranked qualitative hypothesis naming the plant types most and least favoured by urban land use.

THREE ADDITIONS
A. Confounder report is mandatory, not optional. Urban.2009.1000m correlates −0.53 with elevation and +0.51 with temperature, so run the baseline urban-only model and the covariate-adjusted model (elevation, temperature, rainfall, distance.road, distance.stream) side by side for each pathway, and report how much the urban slope moves. If the pathway interaction disappears after adjustment, that is the finding, not an inconvenience. Include VIFs.

INSPECTION COMPLETE (no models run). The two main CSVs are NOT joinable at row level — only the pathway vocabulary, the plot network concept, and the 81/81 tree join are shared.

**1a. invasion_success_pathways.csv — 81 rows x 19 cols (species-level, comma-delimited)**
- 77 unique species; 4 appear twice (duplicated TRUE = 4 rows / FALSE = 77): Eucalyptus camaldulensis, Opuntia ficus-indica, Oxalis debilis, Populus deltoides. The duplicate rows carry the "species.relative" labels and have tip labels suffixed "2", so the tree legitimately has 81 tips for 77 species.
- Missing only in genus.relative (79 NA; filled Calamagrostis, Rheum) and species.relative (77 NA; the 4 reference species). All other columns complete.
- Factors: intro.pathway Gardening 42 / Unintentional 30 / AgriForest 9; growth.form Perennial fg 30 / Shrub-tree 27 / Annual fg 24; dispersal Unspecific 42 / Animal 21 / Wind 18; vegetative Yes 35 / No 46; 33 families (Asteraceae 14, Poaceae 10, Amaranthaceae 7).
- Numerics: number.of.invaded.plots 1-53 (sum 472; 452 dropping duplicated rows), area.of.occupancy.10km 1-25, habitat.range 1-7, invaded.niche.breadth 0-1.759, native.niche.breadth 0.262-1.248, mrt 6-250 yr, height 0.04-40 m.

**1b. invaded_niche_pathways.csv — 632 rows x 37 cols, ZERO missing, TAB-delimited**
Your read is correct with three corrections. Rows are unique plots (632 unique lon/lat pairs, no duplicates, no plot-ID column; integer UTM-31N-like coords E 368,645-481,175 / N 4,562,825-4,684,875, ~110x120 km; median nearest-neighbour 1,316 m). Habitat = 10 classes: Scrublands 106, Croplands 92, Coniferous forests 77, Broad-leaved forests 68, Urban 65, Riparian 61, Rock outcrops 57, Meadows 39, Wetlands 38, Coastal 29.
Corrections: (i) the 18 land-cover columns ({cropland,urban} x {1956,1993,2009} x {50,500,1000 m}) are FRACTIONS 0-1, not percentages as the metadata claims (all maxima 1.00); (ii) the progressive/regressive/no.changes columns exist ONLY for the 50 m buffer (1956-2009 and 1993-2009) and are fractional shares of buffer area, not binary classes (row sums ~1: exactly 1.00 in 503/632, rounding elsewhere; 4 rows all-zero = never urban/cropland); (iii) there are 5 other predictors: elevation, distance.stream, distance.road, annual.temperature/rainfall/radiation.

**1c. Meaning/unit of n.gard / n.unint / n.agfo**
Per-PLOT introduced-species richness split by introduction pathway (integers). Identity n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo == n.total holds for 632/632 rows. Unit = species per plot, NOT frequency of introduction events (the metadata wording is misleading). Column totals: gard 169, unint 289, agfo 23, total 481 plot x species records. Extreme rarity: 69.8% of plots have n.total=0; n.gard 81.5% zeros; n.unint 77.1% zeros; n.agfo 96.7% zeros (AgriForest present in only 21 of 632 plots, 23 records total). Variance/mean 1.14-2.92 (mild overdispersion). Habitat and urban cover are partly confounded: mean urban.2009.1000m = 0.50 in "Urban" habitat vs 0.03 in Meadows/Rock outcrops, yet 116 non-Urban-habitat plots also exceed 10% urban at 500 m — habitat must stay as a covariate.

**1d. temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv — 12 rows = 4 periods x 3 pathways + n (TAB-delimited)**
N = 1,046 species-records (regional Catalonia catalogue; ~13x the 77 species in the plot dataset). Within-period %: AgriForest 51.4 -> 29.8 -> 13.1 -> 6.1; Gardening 16.8 -> 44.6 -> 49.0 -> 75.2; Unintentional 31.8 -> 25.6 -> 37.9 -> 18.8 (Before 1500 -> 1985-2019). Chi2 = 230.4, dof = 6, p ~ 6e-47. It shares NO key with the other files. FLAGGED AS CONTEXT ONLY per your instruction: it evidences a pathway shift over time, not an urban effect. A derived cross-check (intro year ~ 2019 - mrt for the 77 local species) reproduces the same qualitative pattern (Gardening ~78% of post-1984 local species), but that depends on an assumed reference year, so it is corroboration, not a test.

**1e. Tree join: 81/81 EXACT match between phylogenetic_tree.txt tips and phylo.tip.label, zero mismatch in either direction.** Ultrametric time tree (all root-to-tip depths 325.050), 20 labelled internal nodes (Open Tree of Life "mrcaott..." clade labels). Caution: binomialising Scientific_name matches only 76/81 (author citations + the "...2" duplicate labels), so phylo.tip.label is the only valid join key.

**Linkage verdict:** no plot ID and no species names in the niche file, habitat labels only there. Margins roughly agree (niche 169/289/23 = 481 vs species-file number.of.invaded.plots 163/288/21 = 472, or 452 for unique species), implying the same plot network but a residual ~20-30-record difference. Link is at pathway-label + shared-plot-network level, NOT species x plot, so species-specific urban niches are not identifiable.

**2. Proposed approach.** (a) Urbanization per PLOT (current cover at 3 buffers/3 years + 1956->2009 and 1993->2009 deltas); species-level urbanization is not observable. (b) "Types" = introduction pathway primary; growth form, dispersal, vegetative, height, mrt secondary. (c) Response = plot-level n.gard / n.unint / n.agfo (+n.total), because that is the ONLY variable where pathway identity coexists with plot-level urban cover and change, enabling a formal pathway x urban interaction and a pathway-composition model. Rejected as primary: number.of.invaded.plots and area.of.occupancy (species-level, no urban exposure; kept for a secondary spread comparison), niche breadths (no urban covariate per species), total richness alone (destroys the pathway contrast the question asks for). Primary spec fixed in advance: negative-binomial / zero-inflated-Poisson counts of each pathway ~ log(urban.2009.500m+0.01) + cropland.2009.500m + elevation + annual.temperature + distance.road, with habitat as stratum/covariate; plus a multinomial / Dirichlet-multinomial model of per-plot pathway composition given n.total>0 (191 plots) to ask directly whether urban land use shifts WHICH type establishes. Sensitivities: all buffers/years, state vs change, +/- habitat, progressive/regressive/no-change shares as categorical alternative, spatial residual check with lon/lat smooths. Secondary species-level: NB model number.of.invaded.plots ~ pathway + growth.form + dispersal + vegetative + mrt (mrt mandatory since residence time drives spread), optional PGLS on the 81-tip tree. Deliverable: data-grounded hypothesis + executed script.

**3. Assumptions vs unknowns** are listed in the structured fields; the decisive limitation is that AgriForest (23 records, 21 plots, 9 species) is likely descriptive-only, so the sharpest inference is a Gardening-vs-Unintentional contrast plus the composition model.

assumptions: urban.* and cropland.* are fractions 0-1 despite metadata saying percentage; treated as cover proportions.
Each niche-file row is one sampled vegetation plot (632 unique coordinates, no plot ID); plot size, survey effort and survey year assumed constant since no effort column exists.
n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo are per-plot pathway richness from the same plot network that produced number.of.invaded.plots (supported by matching margins 481 vs 472).
Types of introduced plants = introduction pathway primary, growth.form/dispersal/vegetative/height/mrt secondary (as you proposed).
Urban land use = urban cover in plot buffers plus its multi-decadal change; the species file has no urban exposure variable at all.
duplicated=TRUE rows are reference rows for relative comparisons: species-level analyses use 77 unique species, with the 81-row variant as sensitivity.
Reference year 2019 for converting mrt to an introduction year is an assumption used only in the temporal context cross-check.
Response variable = plot-level pathway richness (n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo, n.total); number.of.invaded.plots and area.of.occupancy serve only as secondary spread measures.
uncertainties: Whether the per-plot n.* counts include only the 77 trait-listed species or a broader introduced flora; the 9-29 record margin between the files cannot be resolved without a species-by-plot matrix.

AgriForest may simply not be testable at plot level (23 records in 21 plots, 9 species) - expect descriptive-only status with very wide CIs, pushing primary inference onto the Gardening vs Unintentional contrast plus composition modelling.

The flora is a single time slice, so urbanisation cannot be modelled as a process over time; only spatial contrasts (urban cover, land-cover delta, progressive/regressive shares) exist. urban.1993 vs urban.2009 are r=0.92 apart, so 'recent' vs 'historical' urbanisation is weakly identified.

Confounding: urban cover correlates with temperature (0.46) and elevation (-0.48), and urban change anti-correlates with cropland change (-0.82); separating urbanisation from climate/elevation and from cropland abandonment is a genuine identification problem.
Habitat class 'Urban' vs continuous urban cover are competing operationalisations (61/65 Urban-habitat plots exceed 10% urban at 500 m, but 116 other plots do too) - specification-dependent results.

Sampling design: it is unknown whether plots were sited with respect to disturbance; if so, urban effect and plot availability are confounded and only partly controllable via distance.road plus spatial smooths (median nearest-neighbour 1.3 km implies spatial autocorrelation).
Scope mismatch: temporal table is Catalonia-wide (N=1,046) while plot data are Barcelona province (77 species), so the pathway shift is background, not evidence on urban effects.

Whether phylogeny adds anything beyond robustness: the tree joins perfectly, but because no species-level urban exposure exists, PGLS can only test whether pathway differences in spread are phylogenetic artefacts.
Zero-inflation handling: 69.8% structural zeros in n.total; ZIP vs hurdle vs NB choice could change significance for the rare pathways and should be pre-specified.
No agreed multiple-testing budget: 3 pathways x 3 buffers x 3 years invites specification shopping, which is why the primary specification above is fixed before fitting.

Evalúa exceso de ceros (70% n.total=0) y, si NB no basta, pasa a hurdle/ZIP y repórtalo explícitamente. Habitat como efecto aleatorio; si el ajuste es inestable con 10 niveles, usa fixed effect y dilo.

2) Predictor principal: urban.2009.50m. Justifica la elección con tus propios números (75% de parcelas con cero urbano a 50 m es preocupante) y añade como robustez urban.2009.500m y 1000m, más 1956 y 1993 (una combinación año×buffer por modelo, nunca juntas por la colinealidad 0.90 que detectaste). Cropland, progressive/regressive, log1p(distance.road), log1p(distance.stream), elevation y clima como covariables; revisa VIF antes de interpretar.

3) Compara el tamaño del efecto urbano ENTRE pathways en el mismo marco (por ejemplo modelos con interacción urban×pathway o contraste de coeficientes con bootstrap). Esto es lo central para la pregunta: "¿el efecto fue distinto según el tipo de planta?". No me quedes solo en coeficientes significados por separado.

4) Robustez obligatoria: repetir excluyendo habitat "Urban" (65 parcelas, urban.2009.50m medio 0.689 vs 0.045) porque sin eso el resultado puede ser solo una tautología de muestreo. Moran's I sobre residuos y, si hay autocorrelación, PCNM o GRF.

5) Complemento a nivel especie (77 tras excluir duplicated=TRUE): métricas de invasión (log plots, AOO, habitat.range, invaded.niche.breadth) ~ intro.pathway + growth.form + dispersal. Déjalo claro como análisis paralelo, NO como efecto del uso de suelo, porque no hay join especie↔parcela. Filogenia solo como sensibilidad (PGLS manual si es rápido); si se complica, omítela y declara el límite. temporal_trends solo como contexto descriptivo (Gardening 397 en 1985-2019).

6) Idioma de resultados: reportes con números concretos (coeficiente, IC 95%, p, tamaño de efecto en gradientes reales de urbano, no solo por unidad), tabla resumen por pathway y una afirmación final sobre la dirección del efecto urbano por pathway.

Límites que debes mantener en la redacción final: solo asociación, no causalidad; "tipos" = pathways a nivel parcela (growth.form/dispersal no cruzables con urbano); progressive/regressive tratados como cambio genérico de uso de suelo (asunción, no hecho del diccionario). Reporta anomalías reales que encuentres en vez de suavizarlas.

【1. 形状 / 列名 / 缺失】
| 文件 | 行 | 列 | 分隔符 | 缺失 |

| invasion_success_pathways.csv | 81 | 19 | 逗号(CRLF) | 仅 genus.relative 79/81、species.relative 77/81 为 NA，其余 17 列零缺失 |
| invaded_niche_pathways.csv | 632 | 37 | **TAB+引号** | 全 37 列零缺失 |

列名拼写与 datasets.json 完全一致（已逐列核对）。注意：niche 与 temporal 两文件必须 sep='\t'，否则整行被读成一列。

物种表分类变量取值（无 NA）：
- intro.pathway: Gardening 42 / Unintentional 30 / **AgriForest 仅 9**
- growth.form: Perennial fg 30 / Shrub/tree 27 / Annual fg 24；dispersal: Unspecific 42 / Animal 21 / Wind 18；vegetative: No 46 / Yes 35

- **必须纠正你的一条假设：progressive/regressive/no.changes 不是 0/1 指示变量、也不互斥。** 它们是 0.01 网格上的**比例**（各 75–100 个不同取值，如 progressive.1956.2009.50m 有 91 个唯一值，仅 13 行恰为 1，423 行介于 0–1）。三个变量行和：576/632（1956-2009）、580/632（1993-2009）在 0.99–1.01，另有 40、38 行 <0.95（最小 0.00/0.44）；292 行 progressive>0 且 regressive>0 同时成立，283 行三者同 >0。均值 progressive 0.221/0.156、regressive 0.181/0.130、no.changes 0.580/0.703。与实测变化的相关性也很弱（progressive vs urban 500m 变化 r=-0.12；regressive vs cropland 变化 r=-0.24）→ 其确切定义需要你确认（见假设 A3）。

【4. 物种—样地联结】
**不存在。** 四个文件里没有物种×样地矩阵、没有样地 ID 列、没有样地内物种名录；样地表与物种表之间唯一的公共语义是 habitat 类别与"途径"因子。

核对账目：sum(number.of.invaded.plots)=472 vs sum(n.total)=481（差 9）；途径合计 163/288/21（物种表）vs 169/289/23（样地表）→ 两表接近但不完全对账（重复种在物种表被计两次），这也是不要强行合并的证据。

═══════════ 二、分步分析方案（仅方案） ═══════════

S0 预处理与账目：删除 genus.relative/species.relative；断言 n.total=三分量之和；urban/cropland 按 0–1 比例对待；生成 log 协变量、样地空间坐标（UTM）；固化"物种×途径"行的非独立标记。

S1 主分析·样地层面（核心可答部分）
- 响应：n.gard、n.unint、n.agfo（+ n.total）；主预测量：urban.<年>.<缓冲> 比例；分开建模：(a) 存量指标（urban 比例），(b) 变化指标（progressive/regressive/no.changes 比例，或按 A3 二值化）。

- 标准化：n.agfo 仅 23 个出现（96.7% 零）→ 预期只能做 presence/absence 的 logistic 或与其他途径合并（见 A1），不单独解读。

S2 物种层面（回答"哪一类物种受影响更大"的间接证据）

S3 时间趋势（时序吻合性）
- 4×3 列联表：全局 χ² 已可行（230.4, p<1e-45），加 Cramér's V、对应分析（自实现 SVD）给出时期—途径坐标；分途径 2×4 趋势检验/CA 趋势检验；报告园艺占比 16.8%→44.6%→49.0%→75.2%、AgriForest 51.4%→6.1%。

S4 系统发育（备用，条件已满足）

- 缓冲区敏感性：50/500/1000 m × 1956/1993/2009 共 9 组合重复主模型，报告效应量热表（数字表格）。
- 零膨胀/分布敏感性：Poisson vs NB vs 准似然 vs ZINB；仅存在样地子集（n.total>0，n=191）重跑。
- 多重比较：Holm 或 BH-FDR 校正跨途径×跨指标检验；报告未校正与校正后 p。
- 空间自相关：残差 Moran's I（用 UTM 坐标、k 近邻）；若显著则加空间协方差或按生境/区域分层。
- 敏感性：剔除 4 个 duplicated=TRUE 行；剔除 habitat=Urban 的 65 个样地（排除"生境定义本身即城市"的循环）。

S6 综合与提交：把 S1（城市用地 ↑ → 非本土物种丰富度 ↑，且无意引入强于园艺、农林无效应）、S3（园艺引入在近期激增且与城市扩张同期）、S2（途径间入侵力/生态位差异）合成一段自然语言假设，并写明"因缺物种×样地联结，无法识别物种层面的城市暴露"这一限制。

## 1) Inspection Report — actual file संख्याएँ

**File:** `data/meta-regression_joined_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv` — **86 rows × 60 columns** (87 lines including header). `NaN`/`NA` को na_values से पढ़ा गया।

**Project columns — पूरी तरह agree करते हैं:**
| | count |
|---|---|
| project.x = Psychology | 68 |
| project.x = Experimental Economics | 18 |
| project.y = rpp | 68 |
| project.y = ee | 18 |

Cross-tab perfect diagonal है (Psychology→rpp 68, ExpEcon→ee 18), **0 disagreement rows**. यानि project.x/project.y एक ही variable के दो नाम हैं; कोई cleanup ज़रूरी नहीं।

**Discipline counts और project×discipline cross-tab:**
| discipline | Economics | Psychology | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cognitive | 0 | 34 | **34** |
| Social | 0 | 34 | **34** |
| Economics | 18 | 0 | **18** |

→ Discipline project से nested है: Economics ≡ पूरा ee project; Cognitive/Social पूरे Psychology। यानि 3-level discipline = 2-level project से ज़्यादा informative (Psychology को Cognitive vs Social में तोड़ता है)।

**Missingness मुख्य effect columns की — शून्य:**
`ro, rr, fiso, fisr, se_fiso, se_fisr, relative_es, replicated, no, nr, n.r, power.o, power.r, power_planned.r` = **0% NaN** (सभी 86 rows complete, project और discipline दोनों में 0 missing)।
Missing सिर्फ: `pm_belief` 68/86 = **79.1%** (सारे 18 EE rows के पास हैं, 0 Psychology), और `aggregated`/`lab_id` **100% empty** (useless)।

**Duplicates:** 86 unique `study` values, 0 duplicate study, **0 fully-duplicated rows**, 0 duplicated (study+project+ro+rr+no+nr) joined pairs → merge से duplication नहीं आया, grain = 1 study = 1 row।

**Plausibility:**
- `ro`: 0.118 … 0.860, **सभी positive**, कोई |r|>1 नहीं। `rr`: −0.450 … 0.923; **18 rows में rr ≤ 0** (Cognitive 5, Social 10, Economics 3), कोई exact 0 नहीं।
- `se_fiso/se_fisr` सभी >0, और `1/sqrt(n−3)` से **exactly** मेल खाते हैं (ratio = 1.000, min/max भी) → SE analytic हैं, भरोसेमंद।
- `relative_es`: min −0.897, max 2.382; **19 negative**, 13 >1, कोई infinite/undefined नहीं (क्योंकि कोई ro=0 नहीं)। smallest ro = 0.118 (de Clippel AER 2014, N=790) — denominator risk exists पर कोई |ro|<0.1 नहीं; सिर्फ **6 rows |ro|<0.2**।
- `replicated` = 0/1 binary, clean।

**Sample size / power भरोसेमंदता:**
- `no` 6…790 (median 41.5), `nr` 9…1488 (median 59.5), कोई zero/missing नहीं। **5 studies में no < 10** (Cognitive 3, EE 2) — इनमें ro बहुत बड़ा और SE बड़ा, diff अतिशय (e.g. Palmer & Ghose d_fz = 1.17)।
- `n.r` vs `nr`: सिर्फ 6/86 बराबर, corr 0.874 → `n.r` मूल RProjects का अलग/पुराना replication N है; **`nr` use करना है** (यही se_fisr से perfectly consistent)।
- `power.o` 0.31–1.0, `power.r` 0.05–1.0, `power_planned.r` 0.31–1.0 — plausible, पर post-hoc power endogenous है → descriptive के लिए ठीक, primary predictor नहीं।

**Preliminary signal (केवल diagnostics, final analysis नहीं):** overall 84.9% studies में ro > rr; mean (fiso−fisr) = 0.262 ± 0.033। By discipline (unweighted / inverse-variance): Cognitive 0.289 / 0.206; Social 0.233 / 0.208; Economics 0.266 / **0.013 (95% CI −0.05…0.08)।** relative_es median: Social 0.131, Cognitive 0.650, Economics 0.698। ध्यान दें: Economics में unweighted और precision-weighted नतीजा उलटा-सा है (छोटी-N EE studies में diff बड़ा, बड़ी-N EE studies में लगभग शून्य) — यह weighting choice answer बदल सकती है।

## 2) Proposed approach (brief)

- **Grain:** study-level (86 pairs), paired design।
- **Primary outcome:** `d = fiso − fisr` (Fisher-z original − replication), SE_pair = sqrt(se_fiso² + se_fisr²)। Positive d = original > replication।
- **Sensitivity:** (a) `ro − rr` correlation scale; (b) `relative_es = rr/ro` (छोटा = बड़ा shrinkage), median-based + `|ro|>0.2` subset; (c) sign-only share (ro>rr) with exact binomial CI; (d) unweighted vs inverse-variance weighted दोनों report (Economics में यही decisive है)।
- **Groups:** दोनों layers — project (rpp vs ee, 2 levels) और discipline (Social/Cognitive/Economics, 3 levels)। Per-group: mean/median d, paired t-test + Wilcoxon, bootstrap (10k, stratified) CI और SE-based CI, %studies with ro>rr।
- **Weighting/formal model:** fixed-effect inverse-variance weighted mean difference per group; साथ में mixed-effects/meta-regression `d ~ discipline (or project) + 1` weights=1/SE² से discipline differences का direct test; tiny-N (no<10) और |ro|<0.2 exclusion sensitivity।
- **Multiplicity:** pre-registered family = 3 discipline tests + 1 between-discipline regression; Holm correction; exploratory project tests अलग label।
- **Missing-pair handling:** कोई missing pair नहीं (0%), इसलिए कोई imputation/drop नहीं; केवल `pm_belief`/`aggregated`/`lab_id` विश्लेषण से बाहर।
- **Artifacts:** `analysis/meta_regression_analysis.py` (fully executed script) + `analysis/summary_table.csv` (group × estimate × CI × share) + final hypothesis text।
- **Final hypothesis grain:** **दोनों** — primary 3-level discipline (Social, Cognitive vs Economics), और project-level (Psychology vs Experimental Economics) compact statement के रूप में; क्योंकि discipline nested है, यह दोनों का संयोजन सबसे defensible है।

## 3) Consequential assumptions / uncertainties (आपकी confirmation चाहिए)

1. **Domain definition:** मैं discipline (3 levels) को primary मान रहा हूँ, project (2 levels) को secondary। Approve? (नोट: Economics पूरा ee project है, तो "Economics ≡ project" — domain claim project claim से nested रहेगी।)
2. **Weighting:** मेरा default = inverse-variance weighted primary + unweighted sensitivity। पर EE में IV-diff ≈ 0.013 (CI 0 contains 0) जबकि unweighted 0.266 (p=0.007)। अगर आप unweighted/relative_es को primary मानें तो जवाब में Economics भी "larger in originals" की सूची में आ जाएगा; IV primary मानें तो जवाब मुख्यतः Social + Cognitive (Psychology) का होगा। **यह single सबसे consequential choice है।**
3. **relative_es handling:** sign rr के साथ आता है (19 negative), denominator छोटा हो तो inflate (min |ro| = 0.118)। Plan: relative_es को सिर्फ sensitivity के रूप में, median + trimmed + `|ro|>0.2` restricted; कोई hard exclusion primary से नहीं। OK?
4. **Cleanup:** joined file पहले से clean है (0 dup, 0 missing in effect cols) — मैं जैसा है वैसा use करूँगा, सिर्फ `n.r` (purane N) को `nr` से replace नहीं करूँगा, `aggregated`/`lab_id` drop, और no<10 sensitivity flag। कोई extra cleanup नहीं — agree?
5. **Uncertainty:** 86 studies, 3 groups असंतुलित (34/34/18); disciplines project से confounded हैं (Cognitive/Social सिर्फ Psychology में) → discipline-vs-Economics comparison व्याख्यात्मक रूप में project effect से inseparable; power limited, विशेषकर EE n=18।

कोई আপত্তि न हो तो मैं इसी plan पर पूरा analysis चलाकर summary table + final hypothesis दूँगा।
